title.raw: 卷二百零九 列傳第一百三十四 酷吏 Volume 209 Biographies 134: Cruel Officials

sentences.zh: ◎酷吏

translations.literal: ◎ Cruel Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Cruel Officials.

sentences.zh: 太宗定天下，留心聽斷，著令：州縣論死三覆奏，京師五覆奏。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong settled the realm, attentive in hearing cases and passing judgment, and issued regulations: for death sentences in prefectures and counties, three repeated memorials for review; in the capital, five repeated memorials for review.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taizong brought the realm under control, he took care to hear and decide cases himself, and issued regulations requiring three rounds of review before any death sentence in the prefectures and counties, and five in the capital.

sentences.zh: 獄已決，尚芋然為徹膳止樂。

translations.literal: Even after cases were decided, he still remained apprehensive, withdrawing meals and stopping music.
translations.idiomatic: Even after a case was concluded, he still felt uneasy and would suspend his meal and halt music.

sentences.zh: 至晚節，天下刑幾措。

translations.literal: By his later years, punishments throughout the realm were nearly set aside.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, capital punishment had all but ceased across the empire.

sentences.zh: 是時州縣有良吏，無酷吏。

translations.literal: At that time the prefectures and counties had good officials, and no cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: In those days the local offices had capable administrators and no cruel magistrates.

sentences.zh: 武后乘高、中懦庸，盜攘天權，畏下異已，欲脅制群臣，椔翦宗支，故縱使上飛變，構大獄。

translations.literal: Empress Wu, riding on the feebleness and mediocrity of the emperors Gaozong and Zhongzong, usurped heavenly authority, feared those below who differed from her, wished to coerce and control the hundred officials, and lop off the imperial clan branches; therefore she allowed and sent up secret denunciations and contrived great cases.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu exploited the weakness of the High and Middle Emperors to seize imperial power. Fearing dissent below and seeking to intimidate the court, she cut down branches of the imperial family, and so encouraged secret denunciations and engineered sweeping prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 時四方上變事者，皆給公乘，所在護送，至京師，稟於客館，高者蒙封爵，下者被賚賜，以勸天下。

translations.literal: At that time those from the four directions who reported incidents of treason were all given public carriages, escorted in place wherever they were, brought to the capital, and lodged at guest houses; the high were granted enfeoffment and rank, the low received gifts and rewards, to encourage the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who reported alleged treason from every quarter were given official transport, escorted to the capital, and quartered in guest houses. The most successful won titles and ranks; others received gifts and rewards — all to encourage informers throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 於是索元禮、來俊臣之徒，揣后密旨，紛紛並興，澤吻磨牙，噬紳纓若狗豚然，至叛臠臭達道路，冤血流離刀鋸，忠鯁貴強之臣，朝不保昏。

translations.literal: Thereupon men such as Suo Yuanli and Lai Junchen, divining the Empress's secret intent, rose one after another in multitudes, licking lips and grinding teeth, devouring the girdled sash of officials like dogs and pigs, until the stench of hacked flesh reached the roads, blood of the wronged flowed amid blades and saws, and loyal, upright, noble, and powerful ministers could not count on lasting from morning to evening.
translations.idiomatic: Then Suo Yuanli, Lai Junchen, and their kind, sensing the Empress's secret wishes, sprang up everywhere, hungry as wolves, tearing through the official ranks like dogs at swine — until the stench of butchered flesh filled the roads, innocent blood ran under blade and saw, and even the most loyal and powerful ministers could not be sure of surviving from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 而后因以自肆，不出幃闥，而天命已遷，猶慮臣下弗懲，而六道使始出矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter she therefore indulged herself; without leaving the inner chambers, the mandate of Heaven had already shifted, yet she still feared that her ministers below would not be awed, and so the commissioners of the six circuits first went forth.
translations.idiomatic: She then gave herself free rein. Without leaving the inner palace, she had already taken the throne, yet still feared the court had not been sufficiently terrorized — and so she first dispatched commissioners through the six circuits.

sentences.zh: 至載初，右臺御史周矩諫后曰：「兇人告訐，遂以為常，推劾之吏，以崄責痛詆為功，鑿空投隙，相矜以殘，泥耳籠首，枷楔兼暴，拉脅簽爪，縣發熏目，號曰『獄持』。

translations.literal: In the Zai Chu reign era, Right Censor Zhou Ju remonstrated with the Empress, saying: "Evil men lodge accusations, and it has become routine; the officers who investigate and prosecute take sharp blame and bitter denunciation as merit, bore holes in the empty sky and seek gaps, compete with one another in cruelty, seal the ears in mud and cage the head, cangue and wedge together with violence, pull out ribs and tear fingernails, suspend the hair and fumigate the eyes — called 'Prison Restraint.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zaichu era, Right Censor Zhou Ju admonished the Empress: "Malicious accusers have made denunciation commonplace. Investigating officers treat harsh coercion and venomous slander as achievement — inventing crimes from nothing, vying in cruelty, sealing ears in mud, caging heads, combining cangues and wedges with brutality, pulling ribs and tearing nails, suspending hair and smoking eyes — all under the name 'Prison Restraint.

sentences.zh: 晝禁食，夜禁寐，敲撲撼搖，使不得瞑，號曰『宿囚』。

translations.literal: By day food was forbidden; by night sleep was forbidden; beating and shaking kept prisoners from closing their eyes — called 'Overnight Prisoner.'
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners were starved by day and denied sleep by night, beaten and shaken until they could not rest — this was called 'Overnight Detention.'

sentences.zh: 人茍賒死，何求不得？

translations.literal: If a man may defer death, what request can he not obtain?
translations.idiomatic: Give a man a reprieve from death, and he will confess to anything.

sentences.zh: 陛下不諒，試取告牒判無驗者，使推其情，有司必上下其手，希合盛旨。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not understand: take denunciation documents judged unfounded and have their circumstances pressed — the officials will surely twist both high and low to their hands and seek to accord with your grand intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not see that if you take an accusation already judged groundless and have it investigated anyway, the officials will surely manipulate the case to match what they think you want.

sentences.zh: 今舉朝脅息，謂陛下朝與為密，夕與為讎，一罹攝逮，便與妻子決。

translations.literal: Now the whole court draws breath in fear, saying that your Majesty is intimate with them in the morning and their enemy by evening; once seized and taken, they must part from wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court now holds its breath in terror, believing you are their ally at dawn and their foe by dusk — and that once one is seized, it is a final parting from wife and children.

sentences.zh: 且周用仁昌，秦用刑亡。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhou flourished through benevolence, Qin perished through punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou prospered through benevolence; Qin destroyed itself through harsh law.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察之。」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty examine this."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider this."

sentences.zh: 后寤，獄乃稍息，而酷吏浸浸以罪去。

translations.literal: The Empress came to her senses; prosecutions then slightly subsided, and cruel officials gradually departed through their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress took heed. The great prosecutions eased somewhat, and the cruel officials were gradually removed through criminal charges.

sentences.zh: 天寶後至肅、代間，政事叢，奸臣作威，渠憸宿狡，頗用慘刻奮，然不得如武后時敢搏擊殺戮矣。

translations.literal: From after the Tianbao era through the Suzong and Daizong reigns, government affairs were tangled, treacherous ministers wielded power, veteran slyness and long-standing cunning — punishments were used with some fierce extravagance, yet they did not dare strike and slaughter as in Empress Wu's time.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianbao period through the reigns of Suzong and Daizong, government grew chaotic, wicked ministers threw their weight about, and old hands of cruelty returned — yet even they did not dare kill as freely as in Empress Wu's day.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 非吏敢酷，時誘之為酷。

translations.literal: It was not that the officials dared to be cruel — the times tempted them to cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The officials did not dare cruelty on their own — the age invited it.

sentences.zh: 觀俊臣輩怵利放命，內懷滔天，又張湯、郅都之土苴云。

translations.literal: Look at men such as Lai Junchen, frightened by profit and reckless with life, harboring heaven-reaching guilt within, yet they are but the dregs of Zhang Tang and Zhi Du.
translations.idiomatic: Consider men like Lai Junchen — driven by gain, reckless with lives, guilty beyond measure — yet they are only the refuse of Zhang Tang and Zhi Du.

sentences.zh: 索元禮索元禮，胡人也，天性殘忍。

translations.literal: Suo Yuanli, Suo Yuanli — a non-Han by birth, cruel by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Yuanli — a man of non-Han origin, cruel by nature.

sentences.zh: 初，徐敬業兵興，武后患之，見大臣常切齒，欲因大獄去異己者。

translations.literal: At first, when Xu Jingye's troops rose, Empress Wu was troubled by it; seeing great ministers she often ground her teeth, and wished through great cases to remove those who differed from her.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jingye first rebelled, Empress Wu was deeply alarmed. She would grind her teeth at sight of senior ministers and sought to purge dissent through sweeping prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 元禮揣旨，即上書言急變，召對，擢遊擊將軍，為推使。

translations.literal: Yuanli divined her intent, immediately memorialized reporting urgent treason, was summoned for audience, promoted to General of Irregular Command, and made investigating commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli sensed her wishes, immediately memorialized reporting urgent treason, was summoned for audience, promoted to General of Irregular Command, and appointed investigating commissioner.

sentences.zh: 即洛州牧院為制獄，作鐵籠囚首，加以楔，至腦裂死。

translations.literal: He converted the Luoyang prefectural supervisory office into a specially designated prison, made an iron cage for the head, added wedges, until the brain split and the prisoner died.
translations.idiomatic: He turned the Luoyang prefectural prison into a special interrogation house, fitted an iron cage over the head, and drove in wedges until the skull split and the prisoner died.

sentences.zh: 又橫木關手足轉之，號「曬翅」。

translations.literal: He also used crossbeams to pin hands and feet and turn the body — called "Spreading Wings."
translations.idiomatic: He also pinned hands and feet with crossbeams and twisted the body — a torture called "Spreading Wings."

sentences.zh: 或紡囚梁上，縋石於頭。

translations.literal: Or he suspended the prisoner from a beam and lowered a stone onto the head.
translations.idiomatic: Or he hung a prisoner from a beam and lowered a stone onto the head.

sentences.zh: 訊一囚，窮根柢，相牽聯至數百未能訖，衣冠氣褫。

translations.literal: Interrogating one prisoner, he exhausted every root; mutual implication reached hundreds without finishing; officials' spirit was stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: From a single prisoner he traced every connection until hundreds were implicated and the case still could not be closed; the gentry were utterly broken.

sentences.zh: 后數引見賞賜，以張其威，故論殺最多。

translations.literal: The Empress repeatedly summoned him for audience and rewarded him to expand his terror, hence he condemned to death the most.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress repeatedly received him in audience and rewarded him to magnify his terror, and so he sentenced more people to death than any other.

sentences.zh: 是時來俊臣、周興踵而奮，天下謂之「來索」。

translations.literal: At that time Lai Junchen and Zhou Xing followed in succession and rose — the realm called them "Lai-Suo."
translations.idiomatic: Then Lai Junchen and Zhou Xing rose in his wake, and the realm called them "Lai-Suo."

sentences.zh: 薛懷義始貴，而元禮養為假子，故為后所信。

translations.literal: When Xue Huaiyi first became eminent, Yuanli adopted him as a nominal son, hence was trusted by the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Huaiyi first rose to favor, Yuanli took him as an adopted son, and so won the Empress's trust.

sentences.zh: 後以苛猛，復受賕，后厭眾望，收下吏，不服，吏曰：「取公鐵籠來！」

translations.literal: Later, because of harsh cruelty, he again accepted bribes; the Empress, weary of public expectation, had him taken by lower officials; he would not submit; the official said: "Bring his iron cage!
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his harshness and for taking bribes again, the Empress — disgusted with public outrage — had him arrested. He refused to confess. An officer said, "Bring his iron cage!

sentences.zh: 元禮服罪，死獄中。

translations.literal: Yuanli confessed guilt and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli confessed and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣來俊臣，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen, Lai Junchen — a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen — a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父操，博徒也，與里人蔡本善。

translations.literal: His father Cao was a gambler, friendly with a neighbor, Cai Ben.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cao was a gambler and friendly with a neighbor named Cai Ben.

sentences.zh: 本負博數十萬不能償，操因納其妻，先已娠而生俊臣，冒其姓。

translations.literal: Ben owed gambling debts of several hundred thousand and could not repay; Cao then took his wife — she was already pregnant and bore Junchen, who falsely took Ben's surname.
translations.idiomatic: Ben owed gambling debts of several hundred thousand cash and could not repay them; Cao took his wife — she was already pregnant and bore Junchen, who was passed off under Ben's surname.

sentences.zh: 天資殘忍，喜反覆，不事產。

translations.literal: Cruel by nature, delighting in shifting sides, not attending to property.
translations.idiomatic: He was cruel by nature, fickle, and indifferent to making a living.

sentences.zh: 客和州為奸盜，捕送獄，獄中上變，刺史東平王續按訊無狀，杖之百。

translations.literal: A guest in Hezhou was a robber; captured and sent to prison; in prison he submitted a secret report; the prefectural governor Dongping Wang Xu investigated and found no substance, and flogged him a hundred blows.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling in Hezhou he turned to robbery, was captured and jailed, and filed a secret accusation from prison. Prefect Dongping Wang Xu investigated, found no basis for it, and had him flogged a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 天授中，續以罪誅，俊臣上書得召見，自陳前上瑯邪王沖反狀，為續所抑。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era, Xu was executed for crime; Junchen memorialized and gained audience, stating that he had earlier reported Langye Wang Chong's rebellion but was suppressed by Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou era Xu was executed for crime. Junchen memorialized and gained audience, claiming he had earlier reported Langye Wang Chong's rebellion but had been suppressed by Xu.

sentences.zh: 武后以為諒，擢累侍御史，按詔獄，數稱旨。

translations.literal: Empress Wu found him credible, promoted him repeatedly to Attendant Censor, investigating imperially mandated cases, often pleasing her intent.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu found him credible, promoted him step by step to Attendant Censor, and put him in charge of imperially mandated cases — work that often pleased her.

sentences.zh: 后陰縱其慘，脅制群臣，前後夷千餘族。

translations.literal: The Empress secretly indulged his cruelty, coerced the hundred officials; before and after, more than a thousand clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress secretly indulged his cruelty to intimidate the court, and more than a thousand clans were exterminated before and after.

sentences.zh: 生平有纖介，皆入於死。

translations.literal: In life, the slightest fault all entered into death.
translations.idiomatic: The smallest fault in a man's life was enough to send him to his death.

sentences.zh: 拜左臺御史中丞，中外累息，至以目語。

translations.literal: Appointed Left Censor Director; inside and outside the court all drew breath in succession, until they communicated by eye alone.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Censor Director; inside and outside the court everyone held his breath, communicating only by glances.

sentences.zh: 俊臣乃引侯思止、王弘義、郭弘霸、李仁敬、康韋、衛遂忠等，陰嘯不逞百輩，使飛語誣蔑公卿，上急變。

translations.literal: Junchen then introduced Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Hongba, Li Renjing, Kang Wei, Wei Suizhong, and others — a hundred restless men secretly summoned — to spread flying rumors slandering dukes and ministers, submitting urgent treason reports.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen then recruited Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Hongba, Li Renjing, Kang Wei, Wei Suizhong, and a hundred other restless men to spread slanderous rumors against the high officials and lodge urgent accusations of treason.

sentences.zh: 每擿一事，千里同時輒發，契驗不差，時號為「羅織」，牒左署曰：「請付來俊臣或侯思止推實必得。」

translations.literal: Each time one matter was picked out, the same thing was sent out simultaneously a thousand li away; evidence matched without error — at the time called "entangling fabrication." Documents on the left were annotated: "Please assign to Lai Junchen or Hou Sizhi for investigation — the truth will certainly be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Each time a case was opened, identical accusations were dispatched a thousand li at once, with evidence that matched perfectly — a method called "entangling fabrication." Documents were marked on the left: "Refer to Lai Junchen or Hou Sizhi for investigation — the truth will certainly be obtained."

sentences.zh: 后信之，詔於麗景門別置獄，敕俊臣等顓按事，百不一貸。

translations.literal: The Empress believed it; decreed a separate prison set up at Lijing Gate; ordered Junchen and others exclusively to handle cases — not one in a hundred was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress believed them. She decreed a separate prison at Lijing Gate and ordered Junchen and his men to handle cases exclusively — not one prisoner in a hundred was spared.

sentences.zh: 弘義戲謂麗景門為「例竟」，謂入者例皆盡也。

translations.literal: Hongyi joked, calling Lijing Gate "Cases Concluded," meaning those who entered were invariably finished.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi joked by calling Lijing Gate "Cases Concluded" — meaning that whoever entered was invariably done for.

sentences.zh: 俊臣與其屬朱南山、萬國俊作《羅織經》一篇，具為支脈綱由，咸有首末，按以從事。

translations.literal: Junchen, with his subordinates Zhu Nanshan and Wan Guojun, composed one piece, the "Classic of Fabricating Charges," fully setting out branches, veins, main threads, and causes — each with beginning and end — and handled cases accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen and his aides Zhu Nanshan and Wan Guojun wrote a treatise called the "Classic of Fabricating Charges," laying out in full detail the branches and main lines of every fabricated case from start to finish, and used it as their manual in prosecution.

sentences.zh: 俊臣鞫囚，不問輕重皆註醯於鼻，掘地為牢，或寢以匽溺，或絕其糧，囚至嚙衣絮以食，大抵非死終不得出。

translations.literal: Junchen interrogated prisoners; regardless of severity all poured vinegar into the nose, dug earth for dungeons, or made them sleep in urine and excrement, or cut off grain; prisoners reached gnawing clothing stuffing to eat — generally unless dead they could not finally get out.
translations.idiomatic: When Junchen interrogated prisoners, he poured vinegar into every nose regardless of the charge, dug pits for cells, made men sleep in filth, or cut off their food until they gnawed padding from their clothes to eat — in general, none left alive.

sentences.zh: 每赦令下，必先殺重囚乃宣詔。

translations.literal: Each time an amnesty was issued, heavy prisoners were killed first before the edict was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an amnesty was issued, he killed the gravest prisoners first and only then proclaimed the edict.

sentences.zh: 又作大枷，各為號：一、定百脈，二、喘不得，三、突地吼，四、著即臣，五、失魂膽，六、實同反，七、反是實，八、死豬愁，九、求即死，十、求破家。

translations.literal: He also made great cangues, each with a designation: first, "Stilling the Hundred Vessels"; second, "Cannot Breathe"; third, "Earth-Shaking Roar"; fourth, "Submit at Once"; fifth, "Loss of Soul and Gall"; sixth, "The Fact Is the Same as Rebellion"; seventh, "Rebellion Is the Fact"; eighth, "Dead Pig's Grief"; ninth, "Seek and Immediately Die"; tenth, "Seek and Ruin the Family."
translations.idiomatic: He also devised great cangues, each with a name: "Stilling the Hundred Vessels," "Cannot Breathe," "Earth-Shaking Roar," "Submit at Once," "Loss of Soul and Gall," "The Fact Is the Same as Rebellion," "Rebellion Is the Fact," "Dead Pig's Grief," "Seek and Immediately Die," and "Seek and Ruin the Family."

sentences.zh: 后以鐵為冒頭，被枷者宛轉地上，少遷而絕。

translations.literal: Later he used iron for head caps; those cangued writhed on the ground and in a short while died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he added iron caps for the head; prisoners writhed on the ground and were dead in moments.

sentences.zh: 凡囚至，先布械於前示囚，莫不震懼，皆自誣服。

translations.literal: Whenever a prisoner arrived, instruments of torture were first spread before him to show the prisoner; none did not tremble in fear — all falsely confessed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a prisoner arrived, the instruments of torture were laid out before him first; none failed to quake in terror, and all confessed falsely.

sentences.zh: 如意初，誣告大臣狄仁傑、任令暉、李遊道、袁智弘、崔神基、盧獻等下獄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ruyi, he falsely accused the great ministers Di Renjie, Ren Linghui, Li Youdao, Yuan Zhihong, Cui Shenji, and Lu Xian, and sent them to prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ruyi he falsely accused the great ministers Di Renjie, Ren Linghui, Li Youdao, Yuan Zhihong, Cui Shenji, and Lu Xian and had them imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 俊臣顓以夷誅大臣為功，乃奏囚降制，一問而服者同首，法得減死。

translations.literal: Junchen exclusively took exterminating and executing great ministers as merit; he memorialized that prisoners who, under reduced regulations, confessed at one questioning as if to a leader could by law have death reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen made the extermination of great ministers his special claim to merit. He memorialized that under the reduced-regulation procedure, prisoners who confessed at the first questioning as if to a ringleader could by law have their death sentence reduced.

sentences.zh: 仁傑等已論死，待日而決，稍挺之，仁傑乃遣子持帛書稱枉。

translations.literal: Renjie and the others had already been sentenced to death, awaiting the day of decision; slightly stiffened themselves; Renjie then sent his son holding a silk letter declaring injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie and the others had already been sentenced to death and awaited execution. Holding himself a little straighter, Renjie sent his son with a silk letter proclaiming his innocence.

sentences.zh: 后見愕然，責謂俊臣，對曰：「是囚不褫巾服，何肯服罪？」

translations.literal: The Empress saw it, startled, rebuked Junchen, who replied: "These prisoners have not removed cap and sash — how would they confess guilt?
translations.idiomatic: The Empress read it, startled, and rebuked Junchen. He replied, "These prisoners have not removed cap and sash — how would they confess guilt?

sentences.zh: 后遣通事舍人周綝往視，遽假仁傑襆帶立西廂，綝懼俊臣，東視唯唯去，莫敢聞。

translations.literal: The Empress sent Attendant Palace Gentleman Zhou Chen to inspect; he quickly lent Renjie sash and belt and had him stand in the west wing; Chen feared Junchen, looked east and went off compliantly, none daring to question.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress sent Attendant Palace Gentleman Zhou Chen to inspect. He hastily lent Renjie sash and belt and had him stand in the west wing. Chen feared Junchen, looked eastward, murmured assent, and left — no one dared question further.

sentences.zh: 先是，宰相樂思晦為俊臣夷其家，有子九歲隸司農，上變，得召見，言：「俊臣兇慘，罔上不道，若陛下假條反狀付之，無大小皆如詔。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chancellor Le Sihui had been exterminated by Junchen, who wiped out his house; a nine-year-old son enrolled in the Directorate of Agriculture submitted a secret report, gained audience, saying: "Junchen is ferocious and cruel, deceiving the ruler and violating the Way; if Your Majesty would lend him counter-rebellion charges, great and small alike would follow the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chancellor Le Sihui had been destroyed by Junchen, who wiped out his clan. A nine-year-old son, enrolled in the Directorate of Agriculture, submitted a secret report and gained audience, saying, "Junchen is savage and cruel, deceiving the throne and violating the Way. If Your Majesty would lend him fabricated charges of rebellion, he would make cases of every size fit the edict.

sentences.zh: 臣父死族夷，不求生，但惜陛下法為俊臣所弄耳！」

translations.literal: My father died and my clan was exterminated — I do not seek life, but only pity that Your Majesty's law is being toyed with by Junchen!
translations.idiomatic: My father is dead and my clan exterminated — I do not ask to live, but only grieve that Your Majesty's law is being twisted by Junchen!

sentences.zh: 后意寤，由是仁傑六族皆免。

translations.literal: The Empress's mind awakened; thereby Renjie's six clans were all spared.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress came to her senses, and Renjie's six clans were all spared.

sentences.zh: 又按大將軍張虔勖、內侍范雲仙，虔勖不堪枉，訟於大理徐有功，俊臣使衛士亂斫之，雲仙自陳事先帝，命截其舌，皆即死，人人脅息。

translations.literal: He also investigated Grand General Zhang Qianxu and Inner Attendant Fan Yunxian; Qianxu could not bear false accusation, appealed at the Court of Judicial Review to Xu Yougong; Junchen sent guards to hack them chaotically; Yunxian stated he had served the late emperor — ordered his tongue cut off — all immediately died; every man drew breath in fear.
translations.idiomatic: He also prosecuted Grand General Zhang Qianxu and Inner Attendant Fan Yunxian. Unable to endure false accusation, Qianxu appealed to Xu Yougong at the Court of Judicial Review. Junchen sent guards to hack them to pieces. Yunxian declared that he had served the late emperor — they cut out his tongue — and both died on the spot. Everyone held his breath in terror.

sentences.zh: 久之，俊臣納賈人金，為御史紀履忠所劾，下獄當死。

translations.literal: After a long time, Junchen accepted a merchant's gold, was impeached by Censor Ji Lvzhong, imprisoned and should die.
translations.idiomatic: In time Junchen took bribes from a merchant, was impeached by Censor Ji Lvzhong, imprisoned, and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 后忠其上變，得不誅，免為民。

translations.literal: The Empress trusted his secret report, was not executed, demoted to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress trusted his secret report, spared him execution, and demoted him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，還授殿中丞，坐贓貶同州參軍事，暴縱自如，奪同僚妻，又辱其母。

translations.literal: In the Changshou era, again appointed Palace Court Director; sat for corruption demoted to Tongzhou military adjutant; unrestrained and violent as before, seized a colleague's wife, again humiliated her mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changshou era he was again appointed Palace Court Director, then demoted to Tongzhou military adjutant for corruption. Violent and unrestrained as ever, he seized a colleague's wife and humiliated her mother as well.

sentences.zh: 俄召為合宮尉，擢洛陽令，進司僕少卿，賜司農奴婢十人。

translations.literal: Soon summoned as He Gong Captain, promoted Luoyang Magistrate, advanced to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, granted ten slaves of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Captain of He Gong, promoted to Luoyang Magistrate, advanced to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and granted ten slaves from the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 以官戶無面首，聞吐蕃酋阿史那斛瑟羅有婢善歌舞，令其黨告以謀反，而求其婢，諸蕃長數十人，割耳剺面訟冤，僅得解。

translations.literal: Because official households had no male attendants, hearing the Tibetan chieftain Ashina Huseluo had a maid skilled in song and dance, he had his faction report her for plotting rebellion to obtain the maid; several dozen chieftains of various tribes cut ears and scarred faces to appeal injustice — barely obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: Because his household lacked a male attendant, hearing that the Tibetan chieftain Ashina Huseluo had a maid skilled in song and dance, he had his faction accuse her of plotting rebellion so he could seize the maid. Several dozen tribal chieftains cut their ears and scarred their faces to plead innocence — and only barely obtained her release.

sentences.zh: 綦連耀等有異謀，吉頊以白俊臣，殺數十族。

translations.literal: Qi Lianyao and others had a different plot; Ji Xu reported to Junchen, who killed several dozen clans.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Lianyao and others had a separate conspiracy; Ji Xu reported it to Junchen, who exterminated several dozen clans.

sentences.zh: 既欲擅發奸功，即中頊以法，頊大懼，求見后自直，乃免。

translations.literal: Wishing to monopolize the merit of exposing treachery, he immediately struck Ji Xu by law; Xu greatly feared, sought audience with the Empress to clear himself, and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to keep the credit for exposing treachery to himself, he immediately moved against Ji Xu under the law. Xu was terrified, sought audience with the Empress to clear himself, and was spared.

sentences.zh: 俊臣誣司刑史樊戩，以謀反誅，其子訴闕下，有司無敢治，因自刳腹。

translations.literal: Junchen falsely accused Judicial Clerk Fan Zhan of rebellion and executed him; his son appealed below the palace gates; officials none dared handle it; therefore he disemboweled himself.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen falsely accused Judicial Clerk Fan Zhan of rebellion and had him executed. Fan's son appealed at the palace gates, but no official dared take the case — so he disemboweled himself.

sentences.zh: 秋官侍郎劉如璿為流涕，俊臣奏與同惡，如璿自訴年老而涕，吏論以絞，后為宥死，流漢州。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Autumn Office Liu Ruxuan wept for him; Junchen memorialized sharing the same evil; Ruxuan appealed that he was old and weeping; officers sentenced to strangulation; the Empress pardoned death, exiled to Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Autumn Office Liu Ruxuan wept for Fan. Junchen memorialized that Ruxuan shared the same guilt. Ruxuan pleaded that he wept because he was old. The officers sentenced him to strangulation, but the Empress pardoned him to exile in Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天中，上巳，與其黨集龍門，題搢紳名於石，抵而仆者先告，抵李昭德不能中。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era, on the shangsi festival, with his faction gathered at Longmen, inscribed official names on stone; whoever was struck down first was to report first; striking Li Zhaode could not hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian era, on the shangsi festival, he gathered his faction at Longmen and carved officials' names on stone. Whoever knocked a name down first was to accuse that man first. They could not hit Li Zhaode's name.

sentences.zh: 或以告昭德，昭德謀繩其惡，未發。

translations.literal: Some reported to Zhaode; Zhaode plotted to bind his wickedness, not yet revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported this to Zhaode. Zhaode plotted to restrain his wickedness, but had not yet acted.

sentences.zh: 衛遂忠雖無行，頗有辭辯，素與俊臣善。

translations.literal: Wei Suizhong, though without conduct, had considerable rhetorical skill, long friendly with Junchen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Suizhong, though a man of poor character, was a skilled speaker and had long been friendly with Junchen.

sentences.zh: 始王慶詵女適段簡而美，俊臣矯詔強娶之。

translations.literal: At first Wang Qingzhou's daughter married Duan Jian and was beautiful; Junchen forged an edict and forcibly took her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qingzhou's daughter had married Duan Jian and was beautiful; Junchen forged an edict and forcibly took her as his wife.

sentences.zh: 它日，會妻族，酒酣，遂忠詣之，閽者不肯通，遂忠直入謾罵，俊臣恥妻見辱，已命驅而縛於廷，既乃釋之，自此有隙，妻亦慚，自殺。

translations.literal: Another day, meeting wife's clan, wine deep, Suizhong went to him; gatekeepers would not pass him through; Suizhong entered directly cursing; Junchen ashamed his wife was humiliated, already ordered driven and bound in the courtyard, then released him; from this there was a rift; the wife also ashamed, killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while entertaining his wife's kin, Suizhong came to visit. The gatekeepers refused him entry; Suizhong burst in cursing. Junchen, ashamed that his wife had been insulted, had Suizhong driven out and bound in the courtyard, then released him. From that there was a breach — and the wife, shamed, killed herself.

sentences.zh: 簡有妾美，俊臣遣人示風旨，簡懼，以妾歸之。

translations.literal: Jian had a concubine who was beautiful; Junchen sent men to convey the implied command; Jian feared and returned the concubine to him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jian had a beautiful concubine. Junchen sent men with a veiled command; Jian, afraid, gave the concubine to him.

sentences.zh: 俊臣知群臣不敢斥己，乃有異圖，常自比石勒，欲告皇嗣及廬陵王與南北衙謀反，因得騁志。

translations.literal: Junchen knew the hundred officials dared not denounce him, then had different designs, often comparing himself to Shi Le, wishing to report the Crown Prince and Prince of Luling conspiring rebellion with the southern and northern yamen, thereby obtaining free rein.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that the officials dared not denounce him, Junchen then harbored other designs. He often compared himself to Shi Le and planned to accuse the Crown Prince and Prince of Luling of conspiring with the southern and northern yamen — thereby winning free rein for himself.

sentences.zh: 遂忠發其謀。

translations.literal: Suizhong exposed his plot.
translations.idiomatic: Suizhong exposed his plot.

sentences.zh: 初，俊臣屢掎摭諸武、太平公主、張昌宗等過咎，后不發。

translations.literal: At first Junchen repeatedly picked at faults of the Wu clan, Princess Taiping, Zhang Changzong, and others; the Empress did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Junchen had repeatedly seized on faults of the Wu clan, Princess Taiping, Zhang Changzong, and others, but the Empress had not acted.

sentences.zh: 至是諸武怨，共證其罪。

translations.literal: At this the Wu clan resented, jointly proved his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Wu clan, resentful, jointly testified to his crimes.

sentences.zh: 有詔斬於西市，年四十七，人皆相慶，曰：「今得背著床瞑矣！」

translations.literal: There was an edict to behead at West Market, age forty-seven; people all congratulated one another, saying: "Now we can sleep with our backs to the bed!
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his execution at West Market. He was forty-seven. People congratulated one another, saying, "Now we can sleep with our backs to the bed!

sentences.zh: 爭抉目、擿肝、醢其肉，須臾盡，以馬踐其骨，無孑餘，家屬籍沒。

translations.literal: Competing to gouge eyes, pluck liver, mince his flesh — in an instant all gone; trampled his bones with horses — not a remnant; household registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: They competed to gouge out his eyes, pluck out his liver, and mince his flesh — in an instant it was gone. Horses trampled his bones until nothing remained. His household was registered and confiscated.

sentences.zh: 方俊臣用事，托天官得選者二百餘員，及敗，有司自首，后責之，對曰：「臣亂陛下法，身受戮；

translations.literal: When Junchen was in power, those who obtained selection through the Bureau of Personnel numbered more than two hundred; when he fell, officials voluntarily confessed; the Empress rebuked them, who replied: "I disturbed Your Majesty's law — my body received execution;
translations.idiomatic: While Junchen held power, more than two hundred men obtained office through the Bureau of Personnel by his patronage. When he fell, officials came forward to confess. The Empress rebuked them. They replied, "I violated Your Majesty's law — let my body be punished;

sentences.zh: 忤俊臣，覆臣家。」

translations.literal: Offend Junchen — overthrow my house.
translations.idiomatic: Offend Junchen — and my house is destroyed.

sentences.zh: 后赦其罪。

translations.literal: The Empress pardoned their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress pardoned their offenses.

sentences.zh: 時有來子珣、周興者，皆萬年人。

translations.literal: At that time there were Lai Zixun and Zhou Xing — both men of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there were Lai Zixun and Zhou Xing — both natives of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，子珣上書，擢左臺監察御史，無學術，語言蚩惡，后倚以按獄，多徇后旨，故賜姓武，字家臣。

translations.literal: In the Yongchang initial year, Zixun memorialized, promoted Left Censor Investigating Censor; without learning, speech coarse and wicked; the Empress relied on him to handle cases, mostly following her intent; hence granted surname Wu, styled Jiachén.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang, Zixun memorialized and was promoted to Left Censor Investigating Censor. Without learning and coarse in speech, he was relied on by the Empress to handle cases, mostly following her wishes; hence she granted him the surname Wu and the style Jiachén.

sentences.zh: 既誣雅州刺史劉行實弟兄謀反，已誅，掘夷先墓，得遷遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Having falsely accused Ya Prefecture Governor Liu Xingshi and brothers of plotting rebellion, already executed, dug up and exterminated ancestral tombs, obtained promotion to General of Irregular Command.
translations.idiomatic: After falsely accusing Ya Prefecture Governor Liu Xingshi and his brothers of rebellion and having them executed, he dug up and destroyed their ancestral tombs and was promoted to General of Irregular Command.

sentences.zh: 常衣錦半臂自異，俄流死愛州。

translations.literal: Often wore brocade half-sleeves to distinguish himself; soon exiled and died in Aizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He often wore brocade half-sleeves to set himself apart; soon he was exiled and died in Aizhou.

sentences.zh: 興，少習法律，自尚書史積遷秋官侍郎，屢決制獄，文深峭，妄殺數千人。

translations.literal: Xing, from youth studied law, from Clerk of the Masters of Writing accumulated promotion to Vice Minister of the Autumn Office, repeatedly decided specially designated cases, language deep and steep, wantonly killed several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xing had studied law from youth, rose from Clerk of the Masters of Writing to Vice Minister of the Autumn Office, repeatedly decided specially designated cases in language harsh and severe, and wantonly killed several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 武后奪政，拜尚書左丞，上疏請去唐宗正屬籍。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu seized government, appointed Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, memorialized requesting removal from the Tang imperial clan register.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu seized power, she appointed him Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing; he memorialized requesting removal from the Tang imperial clan register.

sentences.zh: 是時左史江融有美名，興指融與徐敬業同謀，斬於市。

translations.literal: At that time Left Historiographer Jiang Rong had a fine reputation; Xing pointed at Rong conspiring with Xu Jingye, beheaded in the market.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Left Historiographer Jiang Rong enjoyed a fine reputation. Xing accused Rong of conspiring with Xu Jingye, and he was beheaded in the market.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，請得召見，興不許，融叱曰：「吾死無狀，不赦汝。」

translations.literal: Approaching execution, requested to gain audience; Xing would not permit; Rong shouted: "I die without cause — I will not pardon you.
translations.idiomatic: As execution approached, Rong asked to see the Empress. Xing refused. Rong shouted, "I die innocent — I will not pardon you!

sentences.zh: 遂斬之，屍奮而行，刑者蹴之，三仆三作。

translations.literal: Thereupon beheaded him; the corpse struggled and walked; the executioner kicked it — three falls, three risings.
translations.idiomatic: He was then beheaded. The corpse struggled and walked; the executioner kicked it down — three times it fell and three times it rose.

sentences.zh: 天授中，人告子珣、興與丘神勣謀反，詔來俊臣鞫狀。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era, someone reported Zixun, Xing, and Qiu Shenji plotting rebellion; edict ordered Lai Junchen to interrogate the case.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou era someone reported that Zixun, Xing, and Qiu Shenji were plotting rebellion; an edict ordered Lai Junchen to investigate.

sentences.zh: 初，興未知被告，方對俊臣食，俊臣曰：「囚多不服，奈何？」

translations.literal: At first Xing did not know he was accused; just facing Junchen eating; Junchen said: "Prisoners mostly do not submit — what to do?
translations.idiomatic: At first Xing did not know he had been accused. He was just dining with Junchen when Junchen said, "Prisoners mostly will not confess — what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 興曰：「易耳，內之大甕，熾炭周之，何事不承。」

translations.literal: Xing said: "Easy — put him inside a great vat, fierce coals all around — what matter would he not confess?"
translations.idiomatic: Xing said, "Easy. Put him in a great vat with blazing coals all around — what would he not confess?"

sentences.zh: 俊臣曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Junchen said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Junchen said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 命取甕且熾火，徐謂興曰：「有詔按君，請嘗之。」

translations.literal: He ordered a vat taken and fire kindled, and slowly said to Xing: "There is an edict to investigate you — please try it."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a vat brought and the fire stoked, then said slowly to Xing, "There is an imperial order to investigate you — please taste it yourself."

sentences.zh: 興駭汗，叩頭服罪。

translations.literal: Xing, terrified and sweating, knocked his head and confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Xing broke out in a cold sweat and kowtowed in confession.

sentences.zh: 詔誅神勣而宥興嶺表，在道為讎人所殺。

translations.literal: An edict executed Shenji and pardoned Xing to the Ling region; on the road he was killed by an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Shenji executed and Xing exiled beyond the mountains, but on the way Xing was killed by a personal enemy.

sentences.zh: 神勣者，行恭子，為左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: Shenji was the son of Xing Gong and served as General of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shenji was the son of Qiu Xinggong and held the post of General of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，后使害章懷太子於巴州，歸罪神勣，下遷疊州刺史，俄復故官，佐俊臣等為慘獄，遂見倚愛。

translations.literal: When Gaozong died, the Empress had Crown Prince Zhanghuai harmed at Bazhou, blamed Shenji, demoted him to Prefect of Die Prefecture, soon restored to former office, assisted Junchen and others in cruel prisons, and thereby gained favored trust.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong died, the Empress had Crown Prince Zhanghuai killed in Bazhou and pinned the blame on Shenji, who was demoted to prefect of Die Prefecture but soon restored. He aided Lai Junchen and others in brutal prosecutions and thus won the Empress's favor.

sentences.zh: 博州刺史瑯邪王沖起兵，拜神勣清平道大總管討之。

translations.literal: Bo Prefecture Governor Prince of Langye Chong raised troops; Shenji was appointed Grand Commander of the Qingping Circuit to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chong of Langye, governor of Bo Prefecture, rose in revolt, Shenji was appointed Grand Commander of the Qingping Circuit to put him down.

sentences.zh: 州人殺王，素服出迎，神勣盡殺之，凡千餘族，即拜大將軍。

translations.literal: The prefecture's people killed the prince; wearing plain garments they came out to welcome him — Shenji killed them all, more than a thousand clans in all, and was immediately appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture had killed the prince; when they came out in mourning dress to welcome Shenji, he slaughtered them all — more than a thousand clans — and was immediately made Grand General.

sentences.zh: 侯思止侯思止，雍州醴泉人。

translations.literal: Hou Sizhi — Hou Sizhi, a native of Liquan in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Sizhi was a native of Liquan in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貧，懶不治業，為渤海高元禮奴，詭很無良。

translations.literal: Poor, lazy and not managing his livelihood, he became slave to Gao Yuanli of Bohai — crafty, perverse, and without virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and idle, he became a slave to Gao Yuanli of Bohai — cunning, perverse, and worthless.

sentences.zh: 恒州刺史裴貞笞吏，吏積怨，教思止告舒王元名與貞謀反，付周興鞫訊，皆夷宗，拜思止遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Heng Prefecture Governor Pei Zhen flogged clerks; the clerks nursed resentment and taught Sizhi to report Prince Shu Yuanming conspiring rebellion with Zhen; handed to Zhou Xing for interrogation — all clans exterminated; Sizhi appointed General of Irregular Command.
translations.idiomatic: When Heng Prefecture Governor Pei Zhen whipped his clerks, they nursed a grudge and taught Sizhi to accuse Prince Shu Yuanming of plotting rebellion with Zhen. The case was handed to Zhou Xing for interrogation; entire clans were wiped out, and Sizhi was made General of Irregular Command.

sentences.zh: 元禮懼，引與同坐，密教曰：「上不次用人，如問君不識字，宜對『獬豸不學而能觸邪，陛下用人安事識字？』」

translations.literal: Yuanli feared, drew him to sit together, secretly instructed: "The sovereign uses men out of turn; if asked that you cannot read, you should answer: 'The xiezhi does not study yet can gore evil — why must Your Majesty's men know characters?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli was afraid and drew him aside to a shared seat, whispering, "The Empress appoints people for unusual reasons. If she asks why you cannot read, say: 'The xiezhi needs no schooling to gore the wicked — why should Your Majesty's appointees need to read?

sentences.zh: 無何，后果問，思止以對，后大悅。

translations.literal: Not long after, the Empress indeed asked; Sizhi answered as instructed; the Empress was greatly pleased.'
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Empress did ask; Sizhi answered as coached, and she was delighted.'

sentences.zh: 天授中，遷左臺侍御史，元禮又教：「上以君無宅，必賜所沒逆人第，宜辭曰：『臣疾逆臣，不願居其地。』」

translations.literal: In Tianshou, promoted to Left Censor; Yuanli again instructed: "The sovereign, seeing you without a residence, will surely grant a mansion confiscated from rebels — you should decline: 'Your servant loathes traitors and will not dwell on their ground.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianshou he was promoted to Left Censor. Yuanli coached him again: "The Empress will see you have no house and will surely grant you a mansion seized from some rebel. Decline: 'I detest traitors and do not wish to live where they lived.

sentences.zh: 既而果假之，以其教對，后益喜，恩賞良渥。

translations.literal: Thereupon it came to pass as predicted; he answered per the instruction; the Empress was even more pleased; favor and rewards were very generous.'
translations.idiomatic: When she did offer him such a house, he answered as Yuanli had taught; the Empress was all the more pleased and showered him with favors.'

sentences.zh: 思止本人奴，言語俚下，嘗按魏元忠，讓曰：「亟承白司馬，不爾受孟青。」

translations.literal: Sizhi was originally a slave; his speech was coarse and low; once investigating Wei Yuanzhong, he reproached: "Quickly confess, White Horse Commander — or else receive Meng Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi had been a slave himself, and his speech was vulgar. Once while investigating Wei Yuanzhong he threatened: "Confess at once, White Horse Commander — or take Meng Qing's club.

sentences.zh: 洛陽有白司馬阪，將軍有孟青棒，即殺瑯邪王沖者。

translations.literal: In Luoyang there was White Horse Commander Slope; a general had Meng Qing's club — the same who killed Prince Chong of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had a White Horse Commander Slope, and a general named Meng Qing carried the club that had killed Prince Chong of Langye.

sentences.zh: 元忠不承，思止曳之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong would not confess; Sizhi dragged him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong refused to confess, and Sizhi dragged him along.

sentences.zh: 元忠徐起曰：「我如乘驢而墜，足絓鐙，為所曳者。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhong slowly rose and said: "I am like one who fell from a donkey — foot caught in the stirrup, being dragged along.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong rose calmly and said, "I am like a man who fell from a donkey with his foot caught in the stirrup — dragged along against his will.

sentences.zh: 思止怒，復曳之曰：「拒制使邪？」

translations.literal: Sizhi angrily dragged him again and said: "Resisting the investigating commissioner?"
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi flew into a rage and dragged him again. "You resist an imperial investigator?"

sentences.zh: 欲抵殊死。

translations.literal: He intended to charge him with capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to have him sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 元忠罵曰：「侯思止，欲得我頭，當鋸截之，無抑我承反。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong cursed: "Hou Sizhi — if you want my head, saw it off; do not force me to confess rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong cursed him: "Hou Sizhi, if you want my head, saw it off cleanly — don't force a false confession of treason out of me.

sentences.zh: 汝位御史，當曉禮義，而曰『白司馬』、『孟青』，是何物語？

translations.literal: You hold the rank of censor — you ought to understand ritual and righteousness, yet speak of 'White Horse Commander' and 'Meng Qing' — what manner of speech is this?"
translations.idiomatic: You are a censor and ought to know propriety — yet you bark about 'White Horse Commander' and 'Meng Qing.' What kind of talk is that?"

sentences.zh: 非我，孰教爾邪？」

translations.literal: If not me, who taught you?
translations.idiomatic: If not I, then who taught you that?

sentences.zh: 思止驚汗，起謝曰：「幸蒙公教。」

translations.literal: Sizhi, startled and sweating, rose and apologized: "I am fortunate to receive your lordship's instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi broke into a sweat, rose, and apologized: "I am fortunate to have received your instruction."

sentences.zh: 乃引登床。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led him up onto the couch.
translations.idiomatic: He then escorted Yuanzhong up onto the dais.

sentences.zh: 元忠徐就坐，色不變，獄稍挺。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong slowly took his seat, complexion unchanged; the case gradually slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong seated himself calmly, his expression unchanged, and the prosecution gradually lost momentum.

sentences.zh: 思止音吐鄙而訛，人效以為笑，侍御史霍獻可數嘲靳之，思止怒以聞，后責獻可：「我已用之，何所誚？」

translations.literal: Sizhi's pronunciation was vulgar and mispronounced; people mimicked him for laughter; Censor Huo Xiankai repeatedly mocked and teased him; Sizhi angrily reported it; the Empress rebuked Xiankai: "I have already employed him — why mock?
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi spoke with a vulgar accent that people parodied for laughs. Censor Huo Xiankai repeatedly ridiculed him; Sizhi complained to the Empress, who scolded Xiankai: "I have appointed him — what is there to mock?

sentences.zh: 獻可具奏鄙語，后亦大笑。

translations.literal: Xiankai fully memorialized the vulgar phrases; the Empress also laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankai repeated Sizhi's crude phrases in full to the Empress, who laughed heartily.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣棄故妻，逼娶太原王慶詵女，思止亦請娶趙郡李自挹女，事下宰相，李昭德執不可，曰：「俊臣往劫慶詵女，已辱國，此奴復爾邪？」

translations.literal: Lai Junchen abandoned his former wife and forced marriage to the daughter of Wang Qingshou of Taiyuan; Sizhi also requested marriage to the daughter of Li Ziyi of Zhao Commandery; the matter went down to the chancellor; Li Zhaode held it impermissible and said: "Junchen previously seized Qingshou's daughter — already shaming the state — shall this slave do the same?
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen cast off his wife and forcibly married the daughter of Wang Qingshou of Taiyuan. Sizhi likewise sought to marry the daughter of Li Ziyi of Zhao Commandery. When the matter reached the chancellor Li Zhaode, he objected: "Junchen already shamed the realm by seizing Qingshou's daughter — must this slave do the same?

sentences.zh: 搒殺之。

translations.literal: He was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 王弘義王弘義，冀州衡水人，以飛變擢遊擊將軍，再遷左臺侍御史，與來俊臣競慘刻。

translations.literal: Wang Hongyi — Wang Hongyi, a native of Hengshui in Ji Prefecture, through secret denunciations was elevated to General of Irregular Command, again promoted to Left Censor, rivaling Lai Junchen in cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongyi was a native of Hengshui in Ji Prefecture. Through secret denunciations he rose to General of Irregular Command and then to Left Censor, vying with Lai Junchen in brutality.

sentences.zh: 暑月系囚，別為狹室，積蒿施氈罽其上，俄而死；

translations.literal: In summer months he confined prisoners, setting apart a narrow chamber, piled artemisia and placed felt rugs atop — soon they died;
translations.idiomatic: In summer he locked prisoners in a narrow cell, piled brushwood over them, and covered it with felt — they were dead within moments;

sentences.zh: 已自誣，乃舍佗獄。

translations.literal: once they had falsely incriminated themselves, he then released them to other prisons.
translations.idiomatic: once they had been forced to confess, he transferred them to other jails.

sentences.zh: 每移檄州縣，所至震懾。

translations.literal: Whenever he dispatched proclamations to prefectures and counties, wherever he arrived caused shock and awe.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever his writs reached the prefectures and counties, terror followed.

sentences.zh: 弘義輒詫曰：「我文檄如狼毒、野葛矣！」

translations.literal: Hongyi often boasted: "My documents are like wolf poison and wild kudzu!
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi would boast, "My proclamations are poison — wolf-bane and wild kudzu!

sentences.zh: 始賤時，求傍舍瓜不與，乃騰文言園有白兔，縣為集眾捕逐，畦蓏無遺。

translations.literal: When first lowly, he sought melons from a neighbor and was refused; then he sent up a report saying the garden had a white rabbit; the county gathered a crowd to hunt it; the vegetable plots were trampled without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: When he was still obscure, a neighbor refused him melons from the garden. He filed a report claiming a white rabbit was in the plot; the county sent a crowd to hunt it and trampled every row of vegetables flat.

sentences.zh: 內史李昭德曰：「昔聞蒼鷹獄吏，今見白兔御史。」

translations.literal: Inner Secretary Li Zhaode said: "Formerly one heard of the azure hawk prison officer — now one sees the white rabbit censor."
translations.idiomatic: Inner Secretary Li Zhaode remarked, "We once heard of the 'azure hawk' jailer — now we see the 'white rabbit' censor.

translations.literal: (Closing quotation mark ending Li Zhaode's remark.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of Li Zhaode's remark.)

sentences.zh: 延載初，俊臣貶，弘義亦流瓊州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanzai, Junchen was demoted; Hongyi also was exiled to Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yanzai era Lai Junchen was demoted, and Hongyi was exiled to Qiongzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 自矯詔追還，事覺，會侍御史胡元禮使嶺南，次襄州，按之，弘義歸窮曰：「與公氣類，持我何急？」

translations.literal: He forged an edict to recall himself; the matter was discovered; coincidentally Censor Hu Yuanli was sent to Lingnan, stopped at Xiang Prefecture, investigated him; Hongyi at the end of his rope said: "We are of the same kind — why press me so hard?
translations.idiomatic: He forged an edict summoning himself back, but the fraud was discovered. Censor Hu Yuanli happened to be traveling to Lingnan and stopped at Xiang Prefecture to investigate. Cornered, Hongyi said, "We're birds of a feather — why hound me so?

sentences.zh: 元禮怒曰：「吾尉洛陽，而子御史；

translations.literal: Yuanli angrily said: "I was a prison warden in Luoyang while you were a censor;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli snapped, "When I was warden in Luoyang, you were a censor;

sentences.zh: 我今御史，子乃囚。

translations.literal: now I am censor, you are the prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: now I am the censor and you are the prisoner.

sentences.zh: 何氣類為？」

translations.literal: What sameness of kind is there?"
translations.idiomatic: What 'same kind' are we?"

sentences.zh: 杖殺之。

translations.literal: He beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: He had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 郭弘霸郭弘霸，舒州同安人，仕為寧陵丞，天授中，由革命舉，得召見，自陳：「往討徐敬業，臣誓抽其筋，食其肉，飲其血，絕其髓。」

translations.literal: Guo Hongba — Guo Hongba, a native of Tong'an in Shu Prefecture, served as Assistant Magistrate of Ningling; in Tianshou, through the Gerevolution nomination, gained audience, stating himself: "When formerly campaigning against Xu Jingye, your servant vowed to draw out his sinews, eat his flesh, drink his blood, and drain his marrow.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Hongba was a native of Tong'an in Shu Prefecture and served as assistant magistrate of Ningling. During Tianshou he was nominated through the Gerevolution channel and gained an audience, declaring: "When we marched against Xu Jingye, I vowed to flay his sinews, eat his flesh, drink his blood, and suck out his marrow.

sentences.zh: 武后大悅，授左臺監察御史，時號「四其御史」。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was greatly pleased, appointed Left Investigating Censor; at the time called the 'Four-His Censor.'
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was delighted and made him Left Investigating Censor — nicknamed the 'Four-His Censor' for his four vows of sinew, flesh, blood, and marrow.

sentences.zh: 再遷右臺侍御史，大夫魏元忠病，僚屬省候，弘霸獨後入，憂見顏間，請視便液，即染指嘗，驗疾輕重，賀曰：「甘者病不瘳，今味苦，當愈。」

translations.literal: Again promoted to Right Censor; Chief Minister Wei Yuanzhong was ill; subordinates visited; Hongba alone entered last, worry visible on his face, requested to inspect urine and stool, immediately dipped finger and tasted, tested severity of illness, congratulated: "When sweet the illness does not heal — now bitter in taste — he should recover.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted again to Right Censor. When Chief Minister Wei Yuanzhong fell ill, his staff came to call; Hongba arrived last, feigning deep concern. He asked to examine Yuanzhong's urine and stool, dipped his finger and tasted it, and declared with satisfaction, "Sweet means no recovery — this is bitter, so he will get well.

sentences.zh: 喜甚。

translations.literal: He was extremely pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 元忠惡其媚，暴語於朝。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong loathed his flattery and spoke of it openly at court.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong despised the groveling and denounced him openly at court.

sentences.zh: 嘗按芳州刺史李思征，不勝楚毒死。

translations.literal: Once investigating Fang Prefecture Governor Li Sizheng — unable to bear torture, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Once while investigating Fang Prefecture Governor Li Sizheng, he tortured the man to death.

sentences.zh: 后屢見思征為厲，命家人禳解。

translations.literal: The Empress repeatedly saw Sizheng as a vengeful ghost; ordered the household to perform exorcism.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress repeatedly saw Sizheng's ghost and ordered her household to perform rites of expiation.

sentences.zh: 俄見思征從數十騎至曰：「汝枉陷我，今取汝！」

translations.literal: Soon she saw Sizheng arrive with several dozen riders saying: "You wrongfully framed me — now I take you!
translations.idiomatic: Soon she saw Sizheng ride up at the head of dozens of horsemen crying, "You framed me unjustly — now I come for you!

sentences.zh: 弘霸懼，援刀自刳腹死，頃而蛆腐。

translations.literal: Hongba feared, seized a knife and disemboweled himself to death; presently maggots and rot.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Hongba grabbed a knife and gutted himself. Within moments his corpse was writhing with maggots.

sentences.zh: 是時大旱，弘霸死而雨。

translations.literal: At that time there was great drought; when Hongba died, rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: There was a severe drought at the time; rain fell when Hongba died.

sentences.zh: 又洛陽橋久壞，至是成。

translations.literal: Also the Luoyang Bridge long ruined — by this time it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The Luoyang Bridge, long in disrepair, was finished at the same time.

sentences.zh: 都人喜。

translations.literal: The capital's people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 后問群臣：「外有佳事邪？」

translations.literal: The Empress asked the hundred officials: "Are there good tidings abroad?
translations.idiomatic: The Empress asked the court, "Has anything good happened outside?

sentences.zh: 司勛郎中張元一曰：「比有三慶：旱而雨，洛橋成，弘霸死。」

translations.literal: Director of Merit Evaluation Zhang Yuanyi said: "Recently there are three celebrations: drought ending in rain, Luoyang Bridge completed, Hongba dead."
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhang Yuanyi of the Merit Evaluation Bureau replied, "Three blessings lately: rain after drought, the Luoyang Bridge completed, and Hongba dead."

sentences.zh: 姚紹之姚紹之，湖州武康人。

translations.literal: Yao Shaozhi — Yao Shaozhi, a native of Wukang in Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shaozhi was a native of Wukang in Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初以鸞臺典儀累遷監察御史。

translations.literal: At first through Phoenix Platform ceremonial officer accumulated promotion to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from ceremonial officer of the Phoenix Platform to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，武三思烝僭不軌，王同皎、張仲之、祖延慶等謀殺之，事覺，捕送新開獄，詔紹之與左臺大夫李承嘉按治。

translations.literal: During Zhongzong's reign, Wu Sansi committed incest and impropriety; Wang Tongjiao, Zhang Zhongzhi, Zu Yanqing and others plotted to kill him; the plot was discovered; captured and sent to Xinkai Prison; edict ordered Shaozhi and Left Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhongzong, Wu Sansi was licentious and overreaching. Wang Tongjiao, Zhang Zhongzhi, Zu Yanqing, and others plotted to kill him; the plot was exposed and they were sent to Xinkai Prison. An edict ordered Shaozhi and Left Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia to investigate.

sentences.zh: 初欲原盡其情，會敕宰相李嶠等同訊，執政畏禍，粗滅無所問。

translations.literal: At first he wished to probe the full circumstances; coincidentally an edict ordered Chancellor Li Jiao and others to join interrogation; the ruling ministers feared disaster, roughly suppressed and asked nothing.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shaozhi meant to get the full story, but an edict brought Chancellor Li Jiao and others into the inquiry. The ministers, fearing reprisals, glossed over the matter and asked nothing further.

sentences.zh: 囚呼曰：「宰相有附三思者。」

translations.literal: The prisoner cried: "Among the chancellors are those attached to Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: A prisoner shouted, "Some of the chancellors are in Sansi's pocket!

sentences.zh: 嶠等數附承嘉耳呫嚅，紹之翻然不復顧，即引力士十餘曳囚至，築其口，反接送獄中。

translations.literal: Jiao and others repeatedly leaned to whisper in Chengjia's ear; Shaozhi suddenly would not look back, immediately brought more than ten strongmen to drag the prisoner forth, stuffed his mouth, and sent him back reversed into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao and the others kept whispering in Chengjia's ear. Shaozhi turned on his heel, had a dozen brutes drag the prisoner out, gagged him, and sent him back to his cell.

sentences.zh: 謂仲之曰：「事不諧矣！」

translations.literal: He said to Zhongzhi: "The affair will not succeed!
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhongzhi, "It's over!

sentences.zh: 仲之固言三思反狀，紹之怒，擊折其臂，囚呼天曰：「吾雖死，當訴爾於天！」

translations.literal: Zhongzhi insisted on stating Sansi's rebel conduct; Shaozhi angrily struck and broke his arm; the prisoner cried to Heaven: "Though I die, I shall appeal against you to Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi continued to describe Sansi's treasonous conduct. Shaozhi flew into a rage, struck him, and broke his arm. The prisoner cried to Heaven, "Even in death I will accuse you before Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 因裂衫束之，卒誣以謀反，皆論族。

translations.literal: Thereupon tearing his robe to bind him, finally falsely charged with plotting rebellion — all sentenced to clan extermination.
translations.idiomatic: He tore his own robe to bind the broken arm, then framed them all for treason — every clan was sentenced to extinction.

sentences.zh: 囚等已誅，紹之意岸軒傲，朝野註目，擢左臺侍御史。

translations.literal: After the prisoners were executed, Shaozhi's bearing was lofty and arrogant; court and common people fixed their eyes on him; promoted to Left Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After the executions Shaozhi swaggered with arrogant satisfaction, drawing everyone's gaze; he was promoted to Left Censor.

sentences.zh: 奉使江左，過汴州，廷辱錄事參軍魏傳弓。

translations.literal: On a mission to the lower Yangtze, passing Bian Prefecture, he publicly humiliated Army Records Officer Wei Chuanggong in court.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission south of the Yangtze he passed through Bian Prefecture and publicly humiliated Army Records Officer Wei Chuanggong in open court.

sentences.zh: 久之，傳弓為監察御史，而紹之坐贓，詔傳弓即按。

translations.literal: After a long time Chuanggong became Investigating Censor, while Shaozhi was implicated for bribery; edict ordered Chuanggong immediately to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Chuanggong became Investigating Censor just as Shaozhi was implicated in bribery; an edict ordered Chuanggong to investigate him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 紹之謂揚州長史盧萬石曰：「我頃辱傳弓，今來按，我死矣。」

translations.literal: Shaozhi said to Yangzhou Chief Administrator Lu Wanshi: "I recently humiliated Chuanggong — now he comes to investigate — I am dead.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhi told Yangzhou Chief Administrator Lu Wanshi, "I humiliated Chuanggong not long ago — now he's come to investigate me. I'm a dead man.

sentences.zh: 獄具，得贓五百萬，法當死，韋后女弟救請，故減死，貶瓊山尉。

translations.literal: The case complete — bribery of five million obtained; by law deserved death; Empress Wei's younger sister pleaded for mercy — therefore death reduced, demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Qiongshan.
translations.idiomatic: The case was proved — five million in bribes; by law he should die. Empress Wei's younger sister interceded, so the sentence was reduced to exile as assistant magistrate of Qiongshan.

sentences.zh: 俄逃還京，萬年尉捕擊，折其足。

translations.literal: Soon fled back to the capital; Wannian Assistant Magistrate captured and struck him, breaking his foot.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fled back to the capital; the Wannian magistrate's deputy caught him and broke his leg.

sentences.zh: 更授南陵令，員外置。

translations.literal: Again appointed Magistrate of Nanling, supernumerary placement.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the post of magistrate of Nanling as a supernumerary appointment.

sentences.zh: 開元中，為括州長史同正，不得與州事，死。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, served as Co-Administrator of Kuozhou, not permitted to participate in prefectural affairs — died.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan he was made co-administrator of Kuozhou but barred from governing; there he died.

sentences.zh: 周利貞周利貞者，亡其系。

translations.literal: Zhou Lizhen — Zhou Lizhen — his lineage is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lizhen — his lineage is unknown.

sentences.zh: 武后時調錢塘尉，時禁捕魚，州刺史飯蔬。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's time summoned as Assistant Magistrate of Qiantang; at the time fishing was forbidden; the prefectural governor ate vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he was transferred to be assistant magistrate of Qiantang. Fishing was banned at the time, and the prefect ate only vegetables.

sentences.zh: 利貞忽饋佳魚，刺史不受，利貞曰：「此闌魚，公何疑？」

translations.literal: Lizhen suddenly presented fine fish; the prefect would not accept; Lizhen said: "These are fence-caught fish — why doubt, my lord?
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen suddenly sent fine fish. The prefect refused them. Lizhen said, "These were caught at the weir — why be suspicious, sir?

sentences.zh: 問其故，答曰：「適見漁者，禽不獲，而有魚焉，闌得之。」

translations.literal: Asked the reason, answered: "Just now saw a fisherman — birds did not catch any, yet there were fish — obtained at the fence."
translations.idiomatic: Asked how, he replied, "I saw a fisherman whose nets caught nothing — yet there were fish in the weir."

sentences.zh: 刺史大笑。

translations.literal: The prefect laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，擢累侍御史，諧附權強，五王等疾之，出為嘉州司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, accumulated promotion to Censor; harmoniously attached to the powerful; the Five Princes and others resented him — sent out as Military Administrator of Jia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shenlong he rose to censor, currying favor with the powerful. The Five Princes despised him and had him posted out as military administrator of Jia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武三思亂禁中，五王謀誅之，私語崔湜，湜反以其計告三思。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi violated propriety in the inner palace; the Five Princes plotted to execute him, privately telling Cui Shi — Shi in turn reported their plan to Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi debauched the inner palace. The Five Princes plotted to kill him and confided in Cui Shi, who betrayed the plan to Sansi.

sentences.zh: 五王貶，湜勸速殺之以絕人望，問誰可使，以利貞對。

translations.literal: The Five Princes demoted; Shi urged swift killing to cut off popular hope; asked who could be sent — answered with Lizhen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Princes were demoted, Shi urged killing them quickly to crush any lingering hopes. Asked who should do it, he named Lizhen.

sentences.zh: 利貞，湜內足也。

translations.literal: Lizhen was Shi's intimate insider.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen was Shi's inside man.

sentences.zh: 表攝右臺侍御史馳嶺外，矯殺敬暉、桓彥範、袁恕己，還，拜左臺御史中丞。

translations.literal: Memorialized to act as Right Censor, galloped beyond the ridges, forged orders to kill Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and Yuan Shuji; returned, appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Acting as Right Censor, he raced beyond the mountains and forged orders to kill Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and Yuan Shuji. On his return he was made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 數為仇人狙報，幾不免。

translations.literal: Repeatedly targeted by enemies for ambush and report — barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies repeatedly plotted against him; he barely escaped each time.

sentences.zh: 先天初，為廣州都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantian, served as Regional Inspector of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiantian he became regional inspector of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 湜陷劉幽求謫嶺表，諷利貞殺之。

translations.literal: Shi framed Liu Youqiu, exiled beyond the ridges, and hinted Lizhen should kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had Liu Youqiu banished beyond the mountains and hinted that Lizhen should finish him off.

sentences.zh: 賴桂州都督王晙護而免。

translations.literal: Thanks to Gui Prefecture Regional Inspector Wang Jun's protection, he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was saved only because Gui Prefecture inspector Wang Jun protected him.

sentences.zh: 利貞顓事剝割，夷獠苦其殘虐，皆起為寇，詔監察御史李全交按問，得贓狀，貶涪州刺史。

translations.literal: Lizhen devoted himself to extortion; the Yi and Liao suffered his cruelty and all rose as bandits; edict ordered Investigating Censor Li Quanjiao to investigate — bribery proved — demoted to Prefect of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen devoted himself to extortion. The indigenous peoples suffered his brutality and rose in rebellion. Investigating Censor Li Quanjiao was sent to investigate, proved his graft, and had him demoted to prefect of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元初，詔：「利貞及滑州刺史裴談、饒州刺史裴棲貞、大理評事張思敬王承本、華原令康韋、侍御史封詢行、判官張勝之劉暉楊允衛遂忠公孫琰、廉州司馬鍾思廉皆酷吏，宜終身忽齒。」

translations.literal: In early Kaiyuan, edict: "Lizhen and Fu Prefecture Governor Pei Tan, Rao Prefecture Governor Pei Qizhen, Court of Review Assessor Zhang Sijing, Wang Chengben, Huayuan Magistrate Kang Wei, Censor Feng Xunxing, Judicial Officers Zhang Shengzhi, Liu Hui, Yang Yun, Wei Sui, Zhong Zhongshi, Gongsun Yan, and Lian Prefecture Military Administrator Zhong Silian — all cruel officials — should for life be ostracized and never employed.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kaiyuan an edict declared: "Lizhen, Fu Prefecture Governor Pei Tan, Rao Prefecture Governor Pei Qizhen, Court of Review Assessor Zhang Sijing, Wang Chengben, Huayuan Magistrate Kang Wei, Censor Feng Xunxing, and the judicial officers Zhang Shengzhi, Liu Hui, Yang Yun, Wei Sui, Zhong Zhongshi, Gongsun Yan, and Lian Prefecture Military Administrator Zhong Silian are all cruel officials and shall never again be employed.

sentences.zh: 尋復授珍州司馬。

translations.literal: Soon again appointed Military Administrator of Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again appointed military administrator of Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，授夷州刺史，黃門侍郎張廷珪執奏曰：「陛下英斷聖明，四海心服。

translations.literal: The next year, appointed Prefect of Yi Prefecture; Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Zhang Tinggui submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty is resolute and sagely bright; the four seas submit in heart.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Lizhen was appointed prefect of Yi Prefecture. Vice Director Zhang Tinggui of the Yellow Gate memorialized: "Your Majesty is resolute and sagacious; the realm submits to you in heart.

sentences.zh: 所謂英斷，殄兇逆、正朝廷是也；

translations.literal: What is called resolute judgment is exterminating the violent and rebellious and rectifying the court — that is it;
translations.idiomatic: Resolute judgment means exterminating the violent and rebellious and setting the court right;

sentences.zh: 所謂聖明，辨忠邪、信賞罰是也。

translations.literal: what is called sagely brightness is distinguishing loyal from wicked and trusting rewards and punishments — that is it.
translations.idiomatic: sagacious rule means distinguishing loyal from wicked and keeping faith in reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 利貞，宗、武舊黨，鉏僇桓、敬，自陛下登宸極，布新政，奪其班級，遷之遐荒，以允天下之望，義士猶以罰輕為望。

translations.literal: Lizhen, old partisan of the Wu clan, cut down Huan and Jing; since Your Majesty ascended the imperial throne, spread new governance, stripped their ranks, and moved them to distant wilds to fulfill the realm's hopes — men of principle still regard the punishment as light in hope.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen was an old partisan of Empress Wu's faction who cut down Huan and Jing. Since Your Majesty took the throne, reformed government, stripped such men of rank, and banished them to the wilderness — fulfilling the realm's hopes — men of principle still thought the penalties too light.

sentences.zh: 今錫以朱紱，委以藩維，是絀奸不必行也。」

translations.literal: Now bestowing vermilion ribbons and entrusting him with frontier defense — this is saying that punishing the wicked need not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Now to grant him vermilion ribbons and entrust him with a frontier command is to say that punishing the wicked need not be carried out at all.

sentences.zh: 疏入，遂寢。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; thereupon it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and the appointment was shelved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復授黔州都督，加朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Before long, again appointed Regional Inspector of Qian Prefecture, with added Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lizhen was again made regional inspector of Qian Prefecture and given the rank of Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 廷珪又表還制書曰：「利貞險薄小人，附會三思，傾危朝廷，殺害功臣，人神憤惋，痛毒至今。

translations.literal: Tinggui again memorialized returning the appointment document, saying: "Lizhen is a treacherous, base petty man, attached to Sansi, overturning and endangering the court, killing meritorious ministers — men and spirits rage and grieve; the pain and poison reach to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui memorialized again, returning the appointment document: "Lizhen is a treacherous, contemptible petty man who attached himself to Sansi, endangered the court, and killed meritorious ministers — men and spirits alike rage at him, and the wound is fresh to this day.

sentences.zh: 東都搜掩其家，得金銀錦繡，冒違制令，當加重貶。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital searched and seized his household, obtaining gold, silver, and brocade — violating prohibited regulations and deserving heavier demotion.
translations.idiomatic: A search of his home in the Eastern Capital turned up gold, silver, and brocade in violation of imperial regulations — grounds for a heavier demotion.

sentences.zh: 且久據朝廷，捷給便佞，見忠於君者，猶仇讎然。

translations.literal: Moreover he long held sway at court, quick-witted and sycophantic, treating those loyal to the sovereign like personal enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he had long held sway at court — quick-tongued and sycophantic — and treated those loyal to the throne like personal enemies.

sentences.zh: 使之入朝則亂國，撫俗則傷人。

translations.literal: Let him enter court and he disorders the state; let him govern the people and he harms men.
translations.idiomatic: Bring him to court and he will disorder the state; send him to govern the people and he will harm them.

sentences.zh: 今擢典要藩，繇六品遷三品，何往日罰之，而今日賞之？」

translations.literal: Now elevating him to govern an important frontier — from sixth rank to third rank — why punish him in former days and reward him today?
translations.idiomatic: Now you would promote him to govern an important frontier command, raising him from sixth to third rank — why punish him yesterday and reward him today?

sentences.zh: 玄宗乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong then dropped the appointment.

sentences.zh: 會廷珪罷，起為辰州長史，朝集京師，與魏州長史敬讓皆奏事。

translations.literal: When Tinggui was dismissed, Lizhen was raised to Chief Administrator of Chen Prefecture; at the court assembly in the capital he and Chief Administrator Jing Rang of Wei Prefecture both presented business.
translations.idiomatic: When Tinggui was dismissed, Lizhen was appointed chief administrator of Chen Prefecture. At the capital assembly he and Jing Rang, chief administrator of Wei Prefecture, both presented petitions.

sentences.zh: 讓，暉之子也，以父冤越次而奏曰：「周利貞希奸臣意，枉殺先臣暉，惟陛下正罰以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Rang was the son of Hui; taking his father's wrong, out of turn he memorialized: "Zhou Lizhen, seeking the wicked ministers' intent, wrongly killed my late father Hui — may Your Majesty impose just punishment to answer the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Rang was the son of Jing Hui. Breaking protocol to plead his father's case, he said, "Zhou Lizhen, doing the bidding of wicked ministers, wrongly killed my father. I beg Your Majesty to impose just punishment and answer the realm.

sentences.zh: 左臺侍御史翟璋劾讓不待監引，請行法。

translations.literal: Left Censor Zhai Zhang impeached Rang for not awaiting supervisory escort and requested the law be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor Zhai Zhang impeached Rang for speaking out of turn without waiting for the proper escort and asked that the law be applied.

sentences.zh: 玄宗曰：「訴父之枉，不可不矜也；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said: "Pleading a father's wrong — one cannot fail to pity it;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong said, "A plea for a father's injustice cannot but move one to pity;

sentences.zh: 朝廷之儀，不可不肅也。」

translations.literal: court ritual — one cannot fail to maintain its solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: but court ritual must also be kept solemn.

sentences.zh: 奪讓俸三月，復貶利貞邕州長史。

translations.literal: Rang's salary was stripped for three months; Lizhen was again demoted to Chief Administrator of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped Rang of three months' salary and again demoted Lizhen to chief administrator of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賜死梧州。

translations.literal: Before long, Lizhen was granted death at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lizhen was ordered to take his own life at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元中，又有洛陽尉王鈞、河南丞嚴安之，捶人畏不死，視腫潰，復笞之，至血流乃喜。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan there were also Luoyang Assistant Magistrate Wang Jun and Henan Assistant Director Yan Anzhi — beating men for fear they would not die, seeing swellings burst, beating them again until blood flowed — then they were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan there were also Luoyang Assistant Magistrate Wang Jun and Henan Assistant Director Yan Anzhi, who beat prisoners for fear they might not die. When a swelling burst they beat them again until blood ran — and only then were they satisfied.

sentences.zh: 王旭王旭者，貞觀時侍中珪孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Xu — Wang Xu was grandson of Chief Minister Gui in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xu was the grandson of Chief Minister Wang Gui of the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，為兗州兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, served as Army Records Officer of Yan Prefecture.
