translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shenlong he served as army records officer of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時張易之誅，而兄昌儀先貶乾封尉，旭輒斬其首送東都，遷并州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yizhi was executed, his elder brother Changyi had first been demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Qianfeng; Xu immediately beheaded him and sent the head to the Eastern Capital, transferred to Army Records Officer of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yizhi was executed, his elder brother Changyi had already been demoted to assistant magistrate of Qianfeng. Xu promptly beheaded him and sent the head to the Eastern Capital, and was transferred to army records officer of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長史周仁軌者，韋后黨也，玄宗平內難，有詔誅之，旭不待覆，斬首賫還京師，遷累左臺侍御史。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Zhou Rengui was a partisan of Empress Wei; Emperor Xuanzong quelled the inner turmoil and an edict ordered his execution; Xu did not await confirmation, beheaded him and brought the head back to the capital, accumulated promotion to Left Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Zhou Rengui was a partisan of Empress Wei. When Emperor Xuanzong quelled the palace crisis an edict ordered Zhou's execution; Xu did not wait for confirmation, beheaded him, and brought the head to the capital. He rose through repeated promotions to Left Censor.

sentences.zh: 崔湜敗，其婦翁盧崇道自嶺外逃歸東都，為讎家上變，詔旭訊覆。

translations.literal: When Cui Shi fell, his father-in-law Lu Chongdao fled back to the Eastern Capital from beyond the ridges; an enemy household reported the incident; edict ordered Xu to investigate and confirm.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Shi fell, his father-in-law Lu Chongdao fled back to the Eastern Capital from exile beyond the mountains. An enemy family reported him, and an edict ordered Xu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 旭廣捕親黨，窮極慘楚，當以重辟，崇道及三子皆死，門生故人，並海內名士，皆絓染流徙，天下咨其冤。

translations.literal: Xu broadly captured relatives and partisans, exhausting cruel torture; deserving heavy punishment — Chongdao and three sons all died; students, old friends, and famous men throughout the realm were all implicated and exiled; the realm lamented their wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu swept up relatives and associates and tortured them to the limit. Chongdao and his three sons were all executed, and students, old friends, and celebrated men throughout the realm were implicated and exiled. The whole country lamented the injustice.

sentences.zh: 旭與大夫李傑不平，更相罄訐，傑坐斥衢州刺史，故旭益橫，殘毒以逞。

translations.literal: Xu was at odds with Chief Minister Li Jie; they repeatedly denounced each other to exhaustion; Jie was dismissed and made Prefect of Qu Prefecture — therefore Xu grew more overbearing and indulged his cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Xu feuded with Chief Minister Li Jie, and they denounced each other relentlessly until Jie was dismissed as prefect of Qu Prefecture. Xu then grew even more overbearing and indulged his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 官數遷，常兼御史。

translations.literal: His office was repeatedly transferred; he often concurrently held censorial posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted and usually held concurrent censorial posts.

sentences.zh: 其為人苛急，少縱貸，人莫敢與忤。

translations.literal: His character was harsh and urgent, rarely granting leniency; no one dared oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: He was harsh and unforgiving, and no one dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 每治獄，囚皆逆服。

translations.literal: Whenever he handled cases, prisoners all submitted in reverse.
translations.idiomatic: In every case he handled, prisoners confessed under duress.

sentences.zh: 制獄械，率有名，曰「驢駒拔橛」、「犢子縣」等，以怖下，又縋發以石，脅臣之。

translations.literal: He devised prison instruments, generally all named — such as 'Donkey Foal Pulls the Stake' and 'Calf County' — to terrify subordinates; also suspended hair with stones to coerce confession.
translations.idiomatic: He devised torture devices, each with a name — such as 'Donkey Foal Pulls the Stake' and 'Calf County' — to terrify prisoners, and would suspend them by the hair with stones to force confessions.

sentences.zh: 時監察御史李嵩、李全交皆嚴酷，取名與旭埒，京師號「三豹」，嵩為赤，全交為白，旭為黑。

translations.literal: At the time Investigating Censors Li Song and Li Quanjiao were both severe and cruel; their fierce reputations matched Xu's; the capital called them the 'Three Leopards' — Song the Red, Quanjiao the White, Xu the Black.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censors Li Song and Li Quanjiao were equally brutal, and the capital called them together with Xu the 'Three Leopards' — Song the Red, Quanjiao the White, and Xu the Black.

sentences.zh: 里閭至相詛曰：「若違教，值三豹。」

translations.literal: In lanes and neighborhoods people even cursed one another: "If you break the law, you'll meet the Three Leopards."
translations.idiomatic: In the neighborhoods people even cursed one another, saying, "Break the law and you'll meet the Three Leopards.

translations.literal: (Closing quotation mark.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of the popular saying.)

sentences.zh: 宋王憲官屬紀希虬兄為劍南令，坐贓，旭奉使臨訊，見其妻美，逼亂之，因殺其夫，而納贓數百萬。

translations.literal: An official of Prince Xian of Song, Ji Xiqiao's elder brother, was magistrate of Jiannan and was implicated for bribery; Xu was sent on mission to investigate on the spot, saw his wife was beautiful, forced and violated her, then killed the husband and accepted bribes of several million.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xiqiao's elder brother, an official of Prince Xian of Song and magistrate of Jiannan, was implicated in bribery. Xu was sent to investigate, saw that the man's wife was beautiful, raped her, killed the husband, and accepted bribes of several million.

sentences.zh: 希虬使奴為臺傭事旭，旭不知，頗愛任之，奴盡疏旭請求，積數千以示希虬，希虬泣訴於王，王為上聞，詔劾治，獲奸贓不貲，貶龍川尉，恚而死。

translations.literal: Xiqiao sent a slave to serve as censorate hireling under Xu; Xu did not know, rather favored and trusted him; the slave fully recorded Xu's requests, accumulating thousands to show Xiqiao; Xiqiao wept and complained to the prince; the prince reported upward; edict ordered investigation — illicit bribes beyond counting obtained — demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Longchuan; died of rage.
translations.idiomatic: Xiqiao sent a slave to work as a censorate hireling for Xu, who unknowingly favored him. The slave recorded thousands of Xu's corrupt dealings and showed them to Xiqiao. Xiqiao wept and appealed to the prince, who reported it to the throne. An investigation found untold illicit gains; Xu was demoted to assistant magistrate of Longchuan and died of rage.

sentences.zh: 吉溫吉溫，故宰相頊從子也。

translations.literal: Ji Wen — Ji Wen was nephew of the former chancellor Ji Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen was the nephew of the former chancellor Ji Xu.

sentences.zh: 性陰詭，果於事。

translations.literal: His nature was secretive and crafty, resolute in action.
translations.idiomatic: Secretive and crafty by nature, he was ruthless in pursuit of his aims.

sentences.zh: 諂附貴宦，若子姓奉父兄。

translations.literal: He flattered and attached to noble eunuchs as sons and nephews serve fathers and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He fawned on powerful eunuchs as dutifully as a son serves his father.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，為新豐丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, served as Assistant Magistrate of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he served as assistant magistrate of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 時太子文學薛嶷得幸，引溫入見，玄宗目之曰：「是一不良，我不用。」

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Literary Scholar Xue Yi gained favor and introduced Wen for audience; Emperor Xuanzong looked at him and said: "This is a bad character — I will not use him.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Literary Scholar Xue Yi, then in favor, introduced Wen to the emperor. Xuanzong looked him over and said, "This is a bad character — I won't use him.

sentences.zh: 罷之。

translations.literal: He dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 蕭炅為河南尹，御史遣溫到府有所訊詰，乃並治炅，不為末摋，右相李林甫善炅，故得免。

translations.literal: Xiao Jiong was Henan Intendant; the censorate sent Wen to the office for questioning; he then prosecuted Jiong together, without deferential softening; Right Chancellor Li Linfu favored Jiong, so Wen escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Jiong was Henan Intendant, the censorate sent Wen to his office on an inquiry. Wen prosecuted Jiong as well, without softening his tone toward a superior. Right Chancellor Li Linfu favored Jiong, so Wen escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 炅入守京兆尹，而溫方調萬年尉，不辭，人為寒恐。

translations.literal: Jiong entered to serve as Jingzhao Intendant while Wen was just being transferred to Wannian Assistant Magistrate; Wen did not decline — people were chilled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong became Jingzhao Intendant, Wen was being transferred to assistant magistrate of Wannian under his jurisdiction. Wen did not decline the post, and people were appalled.

sentences.zh: 於是高力士間出就第，炅多私謁，溫乃先往，與力士語，執手歡甚，將出，炅通謁，溫陽惶恐趨避，力士止之，語炅曰：「吾故人也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Gao Lishi came out privately to his residence; Jiong often paid private calls; Wen went first, spoke with Lishi, clasped hands in great joy; as he was leaving Jiong came to call; Wen feigned alarm and hurried aside; Lishi stopped him and said to Jiong: "He is an old acquaintance of mine.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi happened to visit Wen's house privately. Jiong often paid secret calls, but Wen arrived first and chatted warmly with Lishi, clasping his hand. As Wen was leaving, Jiong came to call. Wen pretended alarm and scurried aside, but Lishi stopped him and told Jiong, "He is an old friend of mine.

sentences.zh: 炅揖乃去。

translations.literal: Jiong bowed and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong bowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 它日，到炅府，辭曰：「國家法不敢隳，今而後洗心事公，云何？」

translations.literal: Another day, arriving at Jiong's office, he apologized: "I dare not destroy the state's law; from now on I will cleanse my heart and serve you lord — how will that be?
translations.idiomatic: On another day Wen came to Jiong's office and said, "I dare not violate the law of the state. From now on I will serve you with a clean heart — will that suffice?

sentences.zh: 炅待盡歡。

translations.literal: Jiong treated him with full cordiality.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong received him with every courtesy.

sentences.zh: 林甫與李適之、張垍有隙。

translations.literal: Linfu had a rift with Li Shizhi and Zhang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu was at odds with Li Shizhi and Zhang Ji.

sentences.zh: 適之領兵部，而垍兄均為侍郎，林甫密遣吏擿其銓史偽選六十餘人，帝命京兆與御史雜治，累日情不得。

translations.literal: Shizhi headed the Ministry of War while Ji's elder brother Jun was Vice Minister; Linfu secretly sent clerks to expose more than sixty falsely selected candidates by their appointment clerks; the Emperor ordered Jingzhao and the censorate to investigate jointly — for many days the facts could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi headed the Ministry of War while Zhang Ji's elder brother Jun was vice minister. Linfu secretly had clerks expose more than sixty falsely appointed candidates. The emperor ordered Jingzhao and the censorate to investigate jointly, but for days they could get nowhere.

sentences.zh: 炅使溫佐訊，溫分囚廷左右，中取二重囚訊後舍，楚械搒掠，皆呻呼不勝，曰：「公幸留死，請如牒。」

translations.literal: Jiong had Wen assist in interrogation; Wen divided prisoners left and right in the hall, took two serious prisoners to the rear room for questioning, applied cruel instruments and flogging — all groaned beyond endurance, saying: "My lord, please spare my life — I will confess as the document states.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong had Wen assist in the inquiry. Wen lined prisoners up in the hall, took two serious offenders to a back room, and tortured them with cruel devices until they groaned in agony and cried, "Spare my life, my lord — I'll confess as the indictment says.

sentences.zh: 乃挺出。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were brought forth upright.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched them out.

sentences.zh: 諸史迎懾其酷，及引前，不訊皆服。

translations.literal: The clerks, awed by his cruelty from afar, when brought forward all submitted without questioning.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks, terrified by the spectacle, confessed without even being questioned when brought forward.

sentences.zh: 日中獄具，林甫以為能。

translations.literal: By midday the case was complete; Linfu regarded him as capable.
translations.idiomatic: By midday the case was closed, and Linfu judged him capable.

sentences.zh: 溫嘗曰：「若遇知己，南山白額虎不足縛。」

translations.literal: Wen once said: "If I meet one who knows my worth, the white-browed tiger of the southern mountains is not enough to bind."
translations.idiomatic: Wen once said, "Give me a patron who knows my worth, and not even the white-browed tiger of the southern mountains would be beyond my grasp.

translations.literal: (Closing quotation mark ending Wen's remark.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of Wen's remark.)

sentences.zh: 林甫久當國，權焄天下，陰構大獄，除不附己者。

translations.literal: Linfu long held the state; his power blazed over the realm; secretly he constructed great cases to remove those not attached to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu had long held power, blazing with authority over the realm. He secretly engineered sweeping prosecutions to remove anyone not loyal to him.

sentences.zh: 先引溫居門下，與錢塘羅希奭為奔走，椎鍛詔獄。

translations.literal: First he brought Wen under his patronage, with Qiantang's Luo Xiyi as runners, forging and hammering edict-designated prison cases.
translations.idiomatic: He first took Wen under his wing, with Luo Xiyi of Qiantang as his runner, fabricating cases in the edict-designated prisons.

sentences.zh: 希奭文深虐，其舅鴻臚少卿張博濟，林甫婿也，以姻家故，自御史臺主簿再遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Xiyi was deep and cruel in his documents; his maternal uncle Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Boji was Linfu's son-in-law; through the marriage connection, from Censorate Chief Clerk he was again promoted to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi wrote indictments of deep cruelty. His uncle Zhang Boji, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Linfu's son-in-law, rose from chief clerk of the censorate to Palace Censor through the marriage tie.

sentences.zh: 初，溫因中官納其出武敬一女為盛王妃，擢京兆士曹參軍。

translations.literal: At first Wen, through a eunuch, presented a daughter born to him by Wu Jing as consort to Prince Sheng; promoted to Capital Corps Officer of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wen, through a eunuch, presented a daughter he had by Wu Jing as consort to Prince Sheng and was promoted to capital corps officer of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 林甫欲搖東宮，左驍衛參軍柳勣影會發杜良娣家陰事。

translations.literal: Linfu wished to shake the Eastern Palace; Left Martial Guard Officer Liu Ji, by shadowy coincidence, exposed secret matters of Consort Du Liangdi's household.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu sought to undermine the crown prince. Left Martial Guard Officer Liu Ji opportunistically exposed secret affairs of Consort Du Liangdi's household.

sentences.zh: 溫按狀，勣以誣誅，因引勣所善王曾、王脩己、盧寧、徐征，悉逮縛論死，屍積大理垣下，家屬離竄。

translations.literal: Wen investigated the case; Ji was executed on false charges; thereby implicating Ji's associates Wang Zeng, Wang Xiuji, Lu Ning, and Xu Zheng — all seized, bound, and sentenced to death; corpses piled beneath the walls of the Court of Judicial Review; families scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Wen investigated the case. Ji was executed on false charges, and Wen implicated his associates Wang Zeng, Wang Xiuji, Lu Ning, and Xu Zheng — all seized and sentenced to death. Corpses piled beneath the walls of the Court of Judicial Review and their families fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 初，中書舍人梁涉道遇溫，低帽障面。

translations.literal: At first Secretariat Drafter Liang She met Wen on the road and lowered his hat to cover his face.
translations.idiomatic: Once Secretariat Drafter Liang She met Wen on the road and lowered his hat to hide his face.

sentences.zh: 溫怒，乃諷勣引涉及嗣虢王巨，皆斥逐。

translations.literal: Wen was angry and therefore prompted Ji to implicate She and Heir Apparent Prince of Guo Ju — all were expelled and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was furious and prompted Ji to implicate She and Heir Apparent Prince Ju of Guo — all were driven out and banished.

sentences.zh: 林甫惡楊慎矜，王鉷飛書言圖讖事，委溫以獄。

translations.literal: Linfu hated Yang Shenjin; Wang Hong sent a secret report on prognostic texts and portents; the case was entrusted to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu hated Yang Shenjin. Wang Hong filed a secret report about prognostic texts, and the case was entrusted to Wen.

sentences.zh: 初，慎矜客史敬忠與溫父善，見溫繦葆時。

translations.literal: At first Shenjin's guest Shi Jingzhong was on good terms with Wen's father and had seen Wen in swaddling clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjin's retainer Shi Jingzhong had been friends with Wen's father and had known Wen since infancy.

sentences.zh: 溫馳至東都，捕逮楊氏親屬賓客，取敬忠於汝州，鐵鎖頸，布蒙面，未嘗正視，陰遺吏脅曰：「慎矜獄具，須君一辨，君即服，罪可貸，即不服，死不解。」

translations.literal: Wen galloped to the Eastern Capital, captured Yang clansmen, relatives, and guests, took Jingzhong from Ru Prefecture — iron chains on the neck, cloth covering the face, never looking straight at him — secretly sent an officer to threaten: "Shenjin's case is complete; we need your one word of identification — if you submit, guilt can be pardoned; if you do not submit, death without release.
translations.idiomatic: Wen raced to the Eastern Capital, arrested Yang clansmen, relatives, and guests, and fetched Jingzhong from Ru Prefecture — iron chains on his neck, face covered with cloth, never meeting his eyes. Secretly he had an officer threaten, "Shenjin's case is closed. We need one word from you. Confess and your guilt may be pardoned; refuse and you die without reprieve.

sentences.zh: 敬忠即索筆自款，溫陽不見，再三請，乃與之，對如溫所敕。

translations.literal: Jingzhong immediately asked for brush and wrote his confession; Wen feigned not to see him; repeatedly entreated, then gave it — the response matched what Wen had commanded.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong immediately asked for a brush and wrote his confession. Wen pretended not to notice until Jingzhong begged repeatedly, then gave him the brush. The confession matched exactly what Wen had dictated.

sentences.zh: 溫謝曰：「丈人毋懼！」

translations.literal: Wen apologized: "Elder, do not fear!
translations.idiomatic: Wen apologized, "Elder sir, have no fear!

sentences.zh: 乃下拜。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bowed down.
translations.idiomatic: Then he bowed low.

sentences.zh: 慎矜以左證具，欲自誣，而讖不得。

translations.literal: Shenjin, with supporting evidence complete, wished to incriminate himself, but the prognostic text could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: With the supporting evidence in place Shenjin was ready to incriminate himself, but the prognostic text could not be found.

sentences.zh: 御史盧鉉索其家，挾讖以入，於是慎矜兄弟皆賜死，株連數十族。

translations.literal: Censor Lu Xuan searched his household, smuggling in the prognostic text; thereupon Shenjin and his brothers were all granted death; dozens of clans were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lu Xuan searched his house and planted the prognostic text. Shenjin and his brothers were all ordered to die, and dozens of clans were implicated.

sentences.zh: 是時，溫與希奭相勖以虐，號「羅鉗吉網」。

translations.literal: At that time Wen and Xiyi encouraged each other in cruelty and were called 'Luo's Pincers and Ji's Net.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wen and Xiyi spurred each other on in cruelty and were nicknamed 'Luo's Pincers and Ji's Net.'

sentences.zh: 公卿見者，莫敢耦語。

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers who saw them dared not speak in pairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who saw them dared not speak to one another.

sentences.zh: 溫推事未窮，而先計贓成奏，乃引囚問，震以烈威，隨問輒承，無敢迕，鞭楚未收於壁，而獄具矣。

translations.literal: Wen, before the investigation was exhausted, first calculated the bribes and completed the memorial; then brought prisoners to question, awing them with fierce authority — at each question they submitted, none dared resist; whips and clubs had not yet been hung on the wall and the case was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Before an investigation was even finished Wen would calculate the bribes and draft the memorial, then summon prisoners and cow them with fierce authority until they confessed to every question. Whips had not yet been hung on the wall and the case was already closed.

sentences.zh: 林甫才其為，擢戶部郎中兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Linfu admired his ability and promoted him to Director of the Ministry of Revenue concurrently serving as Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu admired his talent and promoted him to director of the Ministry of Revenue with concurrent service as censor.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠、安祿山方尊寵，高力士居中用事，溫皆媚附之。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong and An Lushan were then highly favored; Gao Lishi held power at the center; Wen flattered and attached to them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong and An Lushan were then at the height of favor, and Gao Lishi held power at court — Wen fawned on them all.

sentences.zh: 兄事祿山，嘗密諗曰：「李右相雖厚待公，然不肯引共政；

translations.literal: He treated Lushan as elder brother and once secretly probed: "Right Chancellor Li treats you generously, yet will not bring you into shared governance;
translations.idiomatic: He treated Lushan as an elder brother and once confided, "Right Chancellor Li treats you well but won't share power with you;

sentences.zh: 我見遇久，亦不顯以官。

translations.literal: I have long received his regard, yet he does not make me prominent with office.
translations.idiomatic: he's kept me around for years without giving me real rank.

sentences.zh: 公若薦我為宰相，我處公要任，則右相可擠矣。」

translations.literal: If you recommend me as chancellor, I will place you in key posts — then the Right Chancellor can be squeezed out.
translations.idiomatic: Recommend me as chancellor and I'll put you in the key posts — then we can squeeze Li out.

sentences.zh: 祿山大悅，亟稱溫才，天子亦忘前語。

translations.literal: Lushan was greatly pleased and urgently praised Wen's talent; the Son of Heaven also forgot his earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was delighted and quickly praised Wen's talent; the emperor forgot his earlier judgment as well.

sentences.zh: 於是祿山領河東節度，表溫自副，並知節度營田、管內采訪，總留事，拜雁門太守，知安邊鑄錢事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lushan held the Hedong command; memorialized Wen as his deputy, concurrently managing circuit garrison farms and internal investigation, overseeing remaining affairs; appointed Prefect of Yanmen, managing frontier coinage.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan then held the Hedong command and recommended Wen as his deputy, with charge of garrison farms and internal investigation, overseeing affairs in his absence. Wen was made prefect of Yanmen and put in charge of frontier coinage.

sentences.zh: 以母喪解，祿山表為魏郡太守。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he resigned; Lushan memorialized him as Prefect of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he resigned mourning, and Lushan recommended him as prefect of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠當國，引拜御史中丞，兼京畿關內采訪處置使。

translations.literal: When Yang Guozhong held the state, he brought Wen in and appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief, concurrently Commissioner for Investigation and Disposition of the Capital Region and Guannei.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong held power he brought Wen in as Vice Censor-in-Chief and commissioner for investigation and disposition of the capital region and Guannei.

sentences.zh: 祿山敕吏設白紬帳於傳以候命，慶緒親御而餞之，溫銜其德，故朝廷動靜輒報，不淹宿而知。

translations.literal: Lushan ordered clerks to set up a white silk tent at the relay station to await orders; Qingxu personally drove out to send him off; Wen bore gratitude for his kindness — therefore he reported court movements at once, knowing within a night without delay.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had clerks set up a white silk tent at the relay station to await his orders. Qingxu personally came to see him off. Grateful, Wen reported every movement at court — Lushan knew within a day.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，祿山入朝，領閑廄使，薦溫武部侍郎以為副。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao Lushan entered court, held the post of Director of the Imperial Stud, and recommended Wen as Vice Minister of War as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 13 Lushan came to court as Director of the Imperial Stud and recommended Wen as Vice Minister of War to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 國忠與祿山爭寵，而溫昵祿山甚，國忠不善也。

translations.literal: Guozhong and Lushan competed for favor; Wen was very intimate with Lushan — Guozhong disliked this.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong and Lushan were rivals for favor, and Wen was very close to Lushan — which Guozhong resented.

sentences.zh: 會河東太守韋陟怨失職，因溫以交祿山，遍饋權近，國忠遣人發其狀，斥溫澧陽長史，其屬員錫及陟皆坐貶。

translations.literal: When Hedong Prefect Wei Zhi resented losing his post, through Wen he cultivated Lushan, broadly presenting gifts to the powerful and near — Guozhong sent men to expose the matter; Wen was expelled as Chief Administrator of Liyang; his subordinate Yuan Xi and Zhi were all implicated and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When Hedong Prefect Wei Zhi resented his loss of office, he used Wen to cultivate Lushan and showered gifts on the powerful. Guozhong exposed the affair; Wen was demoted to chief administrator of Liyang, and his subordinate Yuan Xi and Zhi were demoted as well.

sentences.zh: 明年，溫仍坐受賕、奪民馬，貶端溪尉。

translations.literal: The next year Wen was again implicated for accepting bribes and seizing the people's horses; demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Duanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wen was again convicted of taking bribes and seizing commoners' horses and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Duanxi.

sentences.zh: 始，林甫死，希奭出為始安太守，張博濟、韋陟、韋誡奢、李從一、員錫皆逗留始安，溫既謫，又依希奭以居。

translations.literal: At first, when Linfu died, Xiyi was sent out as Prefect of Shi'an; Zhang Boji, Wei Zhi, Wei Jieshe, Li Congyi, and Yuan Xi all lingered at Shi'an; Wen, once demoted, again relied on Xiyi for residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Linfu died, Xiyi was posted out as prefect of Shi'an. Zhang Boji, Wei Zhi, Wei Jieshe, Li Congyi, and Yuan Xi all lingered there, and after his demotion Wen joined Xiyi.

sentences.zh: 國忠奏遣蔣沇臨按，希奭擅稽罪人，貶海康員外尉，俄遣使者殺溫等五人。

translations.literal: Guozhong memorialized sending Jiang Yan to investigate on the spot; Xiyi was punished for arbitrarily detaining criminals and demoted to Supernumerary Assistant Magistrate of Haikang; soon envoys were sent to kill Wen and four others.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong sent Jiang Yan to investigate. Xiyi was demoted to supernumerary assistant magistrate of Haikang for illegally detaining prisoners. Soon envoys were dispatched to kill Wen and four others.

sentences.zh: 溫之斥，帝在華清宮，詔從臣曰：「溫本酷吏子，朕過用之，故屢構大獄，專威福。

translations.literal: When Wen was expelled, the Emperor was at Huaqing Palace; he told his followers: "Wen was originally the son of a cruel official; I wrongly used him, therefore he repeatedly constructed great cases and monopolized authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen was dismissed the emperor was at Huaqing Palace and told his court, "Wen was the son of a cruel official, and I wrongly employed him. He repeatedly engineered sweeping prosecutions and monopolized power.

sentences.zh: 今既斥，公屬安矣。」

translations.literal: Now that he is expelled, you gentlemen are secure."
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is gone, you gentlemen may rest easy.

translations.literal: (Closing quotation mark ending the emperor's remark.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of the emperor's remark.)

sentences.zh: 溫死五月而祿山反，即偽位，求溫子，方十歲，授河南參軍以報之。

translations.literal: Five months after Wen's death Lushan rebelled; upon taking the false throne he sought Wen's son, just ten years old, and appointed him Henan Army Officer in repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Five months after Wen's death Lushan rebelled. When he declared himself emperor he sought out Wen's ten-year-old son and made him army officer of Henan in repayment.

sentences.zh: 崔器崔器，深州安平人。

translations.literal: Cui Qi — Cui Qi, a native of Anping in Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qi was a native of Anping in Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖恭禮，尚真定公主，為駙馬都尉，貌豐偉，飲酒至斗不亂。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Gongli married Princess Zhending, served as Commandant of the Feathered Forest, appearance ample and imposing, drinking up to a peck without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gongli married Princess Zhending and served as Commandant of the Feathered Forest — a man of imposing build who could drink a peck of wine without losing his composure.

sentences.zh: 器有吏幹，然性陷刻樂禍。

translations.literal: Qi had administrative ability, yet his nature was harsh, scheming, and delighted in others' misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had administrative talent, but his nature was harsh and scheming, and he delighted in others' misfortune.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，舉明經，為萬年尉。

translations.literal: In Tianbao he passed the Mingjing examination and served as Wannian Assistant Magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he passed the Mingjing examination and served as assistant magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 逾月，擢監察御史，中丞宋渾為東畿采訪使，引為判官。

translations.literal: Within a month promoted to Investigating Censor; Vice Censor Song Hun was Commissioner for the Eastern Capital Region and brought him in as judicial officer.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was promoted to Investigating Censor. Vice Censor Song Hun, commissioner for the Eastern Capital region, took him on as judicial officer.

sentences.zh: 渾坐贓敗，器亦廢，後為奉先令。

translations.literal: Hun was implicated for bribery and fell; Qi was also dismissed; later served as Magistrate of Fengxian.
translations.idiomatic: When Hun fell in a bribery scandal Qi was dismissed as well; he later served as magistrate of Fengxian.

sentences.zh: 安祿山陷京師，器受賊署，守奉先。

translations.literal: When An Lushan captured the capital, Qi accepted rebel appointment and guarded Fengxian.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan captured the capital Qi accepted a rebel appointment and held Fengxian.

sentences.zh: 頃之，同羅背賊，賊將安守忠、張通儒亡去，渭上義兵且數萬，器大懼，悉毀賊所署符敕，募眾以應之。

translations.literal: Before long the Tongluo turned against the rebels; rebel generals An Shouzhong and Zhang Tongru fled; righteous troops on the Wei numbered nearly ten thousand; Qi was greatly afraid, destroyed all rebel appointments and orders, and recruited forces to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Tongluo turned against the rebels and rebel generals An Shouzhong and Zhang Tongru fled. Loyalist forces on the Wei River numbered nearly ten thousand. Terrified, Qi destroyed all rebel commissions and raised troops to join them.

sentences.zh: 渭上軍敗，遂走靈武。

translations.literal: The Wei army was defeated; he then fled to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei forces were defeated he fled to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 素善呂諲，得為御史中丞、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Lu Jin and thereby obtained the posts of Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with Lu Jin and through him became Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 肅宗至鳳翔，兼禮儀使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong reached Fengxiang, Qi concurrently served as Commissioner of Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong reached Fengxiang, Qi also served as Commissioner of Ritual.

sentences.zh: 二京平，為三司使。

translations.literal: When the Two Capitals were pacified, he became Commissioner of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were recovered he became Commissioner of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 器草定儀典，令王官陷賊者，悉入含元廷中，露首跣足，撫膺頓首請罪，令刀仗環之，以示扈從群臣。

translations.literal: Qi drafted ritual protocols, ordering court officials who had fallen to the rebels to all enter the Hanyuan Hall court bareheaded and barefoot, beating their breasts and knocking their heads to beg pardon, with blades and staffs encircling them — to show the attending ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Qi drafted the ritual protocol: all court officials who had surrendered to the rebels were to enter the Hanyuan Hall court bareheaded and barefoot, beating their breasts and kowtowing for pardon, ringed by armed guards — a spectacle for the attending ministers.

sentences.zh: 器既殘忍希帝旨，欲深文繩下，乃建議陳希烈、達奚珣等數百人皆抵死。

translations.literal: Qi, being cruel and seeking the Emperor's intent, wished to bind subordinates with severe law, and therefore recommended that Chen Xilie, Daxi Xun, and several hundred others all be punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: Cruel and eager to match the emperor's wishes, Qi sought to bind everyone with harsh law and recommended that Chen Xilie, Daxi Xun, and several hundred others all be put to death.

sentences.zh: 李峴執奏，乃以六等定罪，多所厚貣。

translations.literal: Li Xian submitted a holding memorial; thereupon they sentenced by six grades, with many heavily fined.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian intervened with a memorial, and the court instead sentenced by six grades of guilt, with heavy fines for many.

sentences.zh: 後蕭華自賊中來，因言：「王官重為安慶緒驅脅，至相州，聞廣平王宣詔釋希烈等，皆相顧愧悔。

translations.literal: Later Xiao Hua came from rebel territory and said: "Court officials were heavily coerced by An Qingxu; reaching Xiang Prefecture, they heard Prince of Guangping proclaim an edict releasing Xilie and others — all looked at one another in shame and regret.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiao Hua arrived from rebel-held territory and reported: "The court officials had been driven hard by An Qingxu. When they reached Xiang Prefecture and heard Prince of Guangping proclaim an edict releasing Xilie and the others, they looked at one another in shame and regret.

sentences.zh: 及聞崔器議刑，眾心復搖。」

translations.literal: When they heard Cui Qi's proposed punishments, popular hearts again wavered.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard Cui Qi's proposed sentences, morale wavered again.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕幾為器所誤。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I was nearly misled by Qi."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I was nearly misled by Qi."

sentences.zh: 後為吏部侍郎、御史大夫。

translations.literal: Later he served as Vice Minister of Personnel and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Vice Minister of Personnel and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 上元元年病亟，叩頭若謝罪狀，家人問之，曰：「達奚尹訴於我。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, critically ill, he knocked his head as if confessing guilt; the family asked; he said: "Daxi Yin accuses me.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 1, gravely ill, he kowtowed as if confessing guilt. When his family asked, he said, "Daxi Yin is accusing me.

sentences.zh: 三日卒。

translations.literal: He died three days later.
translations.idiomatic: He died three days later.

sentences.zh: 毛若虛毛若虛，絳州太平人。

translations.literal: Mao Ruoxu — Mao Ruoxu, a native of Taiping in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Ruoxu was a native of Taiping in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 眉長覆目，性殘鷙。

translations.literal: Eyebrows long, covering his eyes; nature cruel and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: His eyebrows were so long they covered his eyes, and his nature was cruel and fierce.

sentences.zh: 天寶末為武功丞，年六十餘。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao served as Assistant Magistrate of Wugong, age over sixty.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao he served as assistant magistrate of Wugong, aged over sixty.

sentences.zh: 肅宗還京師，擢監察御史，以國用大竭，數請掊天下財，巧傅於法，日月有獻，漸見識用。

translations.literal: When Suzong returned to the capital, promoted to Investigating Censor; because state finances were greatly depleted, repeatedly requested extracting the realm's wealth, cleverly applying the law, monthly tributes — gradually recognized and employed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong returned to the capital he was promoted to Investigating Censor. With state finances exhausted, he repeatedly proposed schemes to squeeze wealth from the realm, cleverly cloaking them in law, and brought monthly tributes — gradually winning recognition and appointment.

sentences.zh: 大抵核囚，先收家貲以定贓，有不滿意，攤索保伍姻近，人懼其威，無敢不如約。

translations.literal: Generally when investigating prisoners, first seized family assets to determine bribes; if not satisfied, spread the search to guarantors, neighbors, and relatives — people feared his power and none dared fail to comply.
translations.idiomatic: In investigating prisoners he first seized family assets to fix the amount of bribes; if unsatisfied he extended the search to guarantors, neighbors, and relatives. People feared his power and none dared refuse.

sentences.zh: 乾元中，鳳翔七坊士數剽州縣間殺人，尉謝夷甫不勝怒，搒殺之。

translations.literal: In Qianyuan, Fengxiang Seven Enclosure soldiers repeatedly plundered among prefectures and counties and killed people; Assistant Magistrate Xie Yifu, unable to bear his anger, beat one to death.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyuan, soldiers of the Fengxiang Seven Enclosures repeatedly raided the counties and killed people. Assistant Magistrate Xie Yifu, enraged beyond endurance, beat one of them to death.

sentences.zh: 士妻訴李輔國，輔國請御史孫鎣窮治，獄久不具，詔中丞崔伯陽與三司參訊，未決。

translations.literal: The soldier's wife appealed to Li Fuguo; Fuguo requested Censor Sun Jin thoroughly investigate; the case long remained incomplete; edict ordered Vice Censor Cui Boyang and the Three Offices to join inquiry — undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier's wife appealed to Li Fuguo, who had Censor Sun Jin investigate thoroughly. The case dragged on unresolved until an edict ordered Vice Censor Cui Boyang and the Three Offices to join the inquiry — still without a decision.

sentences.zh: 乃使若虛按之，即歸罪夷甫。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ruoxu was sent to investigate; he immediately pinned guilt on Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu was then sent to investigate and immediately pinned the blame on Yifu.

sentences.zh: 伯陽爭甚力，若虛慢拒，伯陽怒，若虛即馳入白於帝。

translations.literal: Boyang argued fiercely; Ruoxu arrogantly refused; Boyang grew angry; Ruoxu immediately galloped in to report to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang argued fiercely; Ruoxu contemptuously refused. Boyang flew into a rage, and Ruoxu immediately raced to the palace to report to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 詔姑出，若虛泥訴曰：「臣出即死。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered him temporarily to leave; Ruoxu clung and petitioned: "If your servant leaves, he dies at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to leave for the moment, but Ruoxu clung and pleaded, "If I leave the palace, I am a dead man.

sentences.zh: 因蔽若虛殿中，而召伯陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ruoxu was hidden in the hall while Boyang was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu was hidden in the hall while Boyang was summoned.

sentences.zh: 伯陽至，具劾若虛罔上，帝主先語，叱伯陽出，並官屬悉貶嶺外。

translations.literal: Boyang arrived and fully impeached Ruoxu for deceiving the sovereign; the Emperor sided with the prior account, berated Boyang to leave, and all his staff were demoted beyond the ridges.
translations.idiomatic: When Boyang arrived he fully impeached Ruoxu for deceiving the throne. The emperor sided with Ruoxu, berated Boyang out of court, and demoted all his staff beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 李峴頗左右鎣等，罷宰相。

translations.literal: Li Xian had somewhat sided with Jin and others; dismissed as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, who had somewhat sided with Jin and the others, was dismissed as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 於是若虛權焰震朝廷，群臣不舒息。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ruoxu's power blazed over the court; the hundred ministers could not breathe easy.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu's power then blazed over the court, and the ministers could not breathe easy.

sentences.zh: 尋擢御史中丞。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，以罪貶賓化尉，死。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, demoted for crime to Assistant Magistrate of Binhua — died.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 1 he was demoted for crimes to assistant magistrate of Binhua, where he died.

sentences.zh: 敬羽敬羽，河中寶鼎人。

translations.literal: Jing Yu — Jing Yu, a native of Baoding in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Yu was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 貌寢甚，性便辟，善候人意。

translations.literal: Appearance very ugly; nature obsequious; good at reading people's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: He was very ugly in appearance, obsequious by nature, and skilled at reading what people wanted.

sentences.zh: 補匡城尉，朔方安思順表為節度府屬。

translations.literal: Appointed Assistant Magistrate of Kuangcheng; An Sishun of Shuofang recommended him as circuit staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant magistrate of Kuangcheng, and An Sishun of Shuofang recommended him as staff on the circuit headquarters.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，擢監察御史，以言利幸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong, promoted to Investigating Censor through profit-speaking favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Suzong's reign he was promoted to Investigating Censor through proposals for profit that won favor.

sentences.zh: 京師平，任遇浸顯，兇態不能忍，乃作巨枷，號「尾榆」，囚人多死。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, appointments gradually became prominent; his violent temperament could not be restrained — he made a giant cangue called 'Tail Elm,' and many prisoners died.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was recovered his appointments grew ever more prominent, and his violent temperament knew no restraint. He made a giant cangue called 'Tail Elm,' and many prisoners died in it.

sentences.zh: 又仆囚於地，以門牡轢腹；

translations.literal: Also prostrated prisoners on the ground and rolled their bellies with a door bar;
translations.idiomatic: He also prostrated prisoners on the ground and crushed their bellies with a door bar;

sentences.zh: 掘地實棘，席蒙上，瀕坎鞫囚，不服則擠之坎，人多濫死。

translations.literal: dug pits filled with thorns, covered with mats, interrogated prisoners at the pit's edge — if they did not submit, pushed them into the pit; many died by wrongful drowning.
translations.idiomatic: dug pits filled with thorns and covered them with mats, interrogating prisoners at the edge — if they would not confess he pushed them in, and many drowned or died unjustly.

sentences.zh: 遷累御史中丞、宗正卿。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotion became Vice Censor-in-Chief and Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Vice Censor-in-Chief and Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 鄭國公李遵坐賄下詔獄，羽參按，遵肥而羽瘠，則引遵危坐小床，痹且仆，遵欲申足，羽曰：「公乃囚，我延公坐，何可慢？」

translations.literal: Duke of Zheng Li Zun, implicated for bribery, entered the edict-designated prison; Yu assisted in investigation; Zun was fat while Yu was thin — he brought Zun to sit precariously on a small bed, numb and about to collapse; Zun wished to extend his legs; Yu said: "You are a prisoner — I offered you a seat; how can you be careless?
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Zheng Li Zun, implicated in bribery, was sent to the edict-designated prison. Yu assisted in the investigation. Zun was stout and Yu was gaunt, so Yu made Zun sit precariously on a small bed until he grew numb and nearly collapsed. When Zun tried to stretch his legs, Yu said, "You are a prisoner — I offered you a seat. How dare you be so careless?

sentences.zh: 遵仆三四，徐受所言，得贓至數百萬。

translations.literal: Zun collapsed three or four times, slowly accepted what was said, and bribes of several million were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Zun collapsed three or four times before slowly accepting what was demanded. Bribes totaling several million were extracted.

sentences.zh: 嗣岐王珍謀反，詔羽窮劾，乃悉召支黨，環以搒具，囚惶怖，一昔獄成，珍賜死，左衛將軍竇如玢等九人皆斬，太子洗馬趙非熊等六七人斃杖下，聞者毛豎。

translations.literal: Heir Prince of Qi Wang Zhen plotted rebellion; edict ordered Yu thoroughly investigate; he summoned all branch partisans, surrounded them with beating instruments; prisoners terrified — in one night the case was complete; Zhen granted death; Left Guard General Dou Rubin and nine others all beheaded; Crown Prince Study Attendant Zhao Feixiong and six or seven others died under the clubs; hearers' hair stood on end.
translations.idiomatic: When Heir Prince of Qi Wang Zhen plotted rebellion, an edict ordered Yu to investigate thoroughly. He summoned all accomplices and surrounded them with beating implements until the prisoners were terrified. In a single night the case was closed. Zhen was ordered to die; Left Guard General Dou Rubin and eight others were beheaded; Crown Prince Study Attendant Zhao Feixiong and six or seven others were beaten to death. Those who heard of it felt their hair stand on end.

sentences.zh: 先是，胡人康謙以賈富，楊國忠輔政，納其金，授安南都護，領山南東路驛事，吏疾之，誣其通史朝義。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Hu man Kang Qian grew rich through trade; Yang Guozhong held government, accepted his gold, appointed him Protector General of Annan, overseeing Shannan East Route relay affairs; clerks hated him and falsely accused him of communicating with Shi Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the merchant Kang Qian, a foreigner, had grown rich through trade. When Yang Guozhong held power he accepted Kang's gold and appointed him Protector General of Annan with charge of the Shannan East Route relay system. The clerks hated him and falsely accused him of communicating with Shi Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 羽鞫之，謙鬚長三尺，明日脫盡，膝腂皆碎，人視之以為鬼，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Yu interrogated him; Qian's beard was three chi long — the next day it was all pulled out, knees and shins all crushed; people viewing him thought him a ghost — then he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu interrogated him. Qian's beard was three feet long; by the next day it had all been pulled out and his knees and shins were crushed to pulp. Onlookers thought they were seeing a ghost. Then he was killed.

sentences.zh: 羽與毛若虛、裴升、畢曜同時為御史，皆暴忍，時稱「毛敬裴畢」。

translations.literal: Yu, together with Mao Ruoxu, Pei Sheng, and Bi Yao, simultaneously served as censors — all violent and cruel; at the time called 'Mao-Jing-Pei-Bi.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu served as censor at the same time as Mao Ruoxu, Pei Sheng, and Bi Yao — all brutal men nicknamed together as 'Mao-Jing-Pei-Bi.'

sentences.zh: 未幾，升、曜流黔中。

translations.literal: Before long Sheng and Yao were exiled to Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sheng and Yao were exiled to Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，羽斥道州刺史，詔殺之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying, Yu was expelled as Prefect of Dao Prefecture; edict ordered his execution.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Baoying Yu was dismissed as prefect of Dao Prefecture and an edict ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 羽聞使者至，缞服而逃，吏械之。

translations.literal: Yu heard the envoy had arrived, fled in mourning dress, and officers shackled him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu heard the envoy had arrived he fled in mourning dress, but officers shackled him.

sentences.zh: 臨死，袖中出牒數番，乃吏相告訐，咤曰：「不及推，死矣，治州者無宜寢。」

translations.literal: Approaching death, he pulled from his sleeve several memorials — clerks denouncing one another — and exclaimed: "No time left to pursue them — I die; those governing prefectures ought not sleep easy."
translations.idiomatic: As he faced death he pulled several denunciations from his sleeve — clerks informing on one another — and cried, "No time to pursue them now — I die, but those who govern prefectures ought not sleep easy.

translations.literal: (Closing quotation mark ending Yu's final words.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of Yu's final words.)
